name: block-row
description: One text block in a list of blocks: the text and, on hover, its actions. Kind "source" is a block to pick (Add; shaded once already used, then Remove in Add's place); kind "editable" has a drag handle, Edit / Delete and an in-place edit mode.

props.name: type
props.description: "source" or "editable".

props.name: text
props.description: The block's text.

props.name: included
props.description: Kind "source": the block is already in the document (row shaded, Remove shown instead of Add; both share one cell so the row keeps its width).

props.name: overlay
props.description: Kind "source": the actions float over the right end of the text on hover instead of taking a column (data-actions="overlay"). Only the button that applies is laid out, so the cell is one button wide and its hover brackets hug the label. The cell runs the row's full height with the button centred, so its fill covers a block of several lines.

props.name: compact
props.description: Kind "source": a shorter row (data-density="compact"): the text with 8px above and below, no 60px minimum, and size="small" Add / Remove buttons one line tall.

props.name: heading
props.description: Kind "source": the block is a section heading of the document (data-kind="heading"); its text is bold; a heading after other blocks has spacing-6 (20px) above it.

props.name: clickable
props.description: Kind "source": data-clickable="true" shows the pointer over the whole row; the host makes a click anywhere on it do what its visible action does (Add or Remove).

rationale: Rows have no hairlines and no vertical rules, unlike table-row: Figma draws these panes as flat block lists on white, each row its text with a trailing blank line, so min-height is spacing.9 + spacing.6 (60px) and padding spacing.cell (10px). Hover and focus-within fill bg.surface-pressed. Actions and the drag icon are at opacity 0 until hover or focus (or edit mode), like table-row's hover-only icons, so a long list reads as text first; keyboard focus keeps them reachable. An already-included source block is shaded (Figma base/warm-100 in light, bg.surface-pressed in dark) and its Add button is visibility:hidden, not removed, so the row keeps its width. Edit mode swaps the text for a textarea with an accent border and drops the text padding, so the box sits where the text was. Drag and drop is driven by the host page through data-dragging (dimmed) and data-drop="before"/"after" (an accent line on the top or bottom edge), the same attribute API table-row offers. Overlay variant (2026-10-19, maintainer, CV referent): the shared Add/Remove cell stretched the Add button to the width of "Remove" and pulled its hover brackets apart. With overlay the actions cell is absolutely positioned over the right end of the text cell (the row is position:relative), shows only the applicable button and takes the row fill by inheritance while visible, so hover and the included shade carry over. Table-row cells (For You) are untouched: the variant is opt-in per row. Not sourced from Figma: the hover / focus reveal of the actions. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Compact (2026-10-19, CV referent): the row loses its trailing blank line (min-height 60px -> none) and takes 8px above and below the text, so a one-line block is 35px; Add / Remove are text-button size="small" (one line tall) so the floating cell sits on the line of text. Heading (2026-10-19, CV referent): a block that is a section heading (Education, Solo exhibitions...) is bold, buttonPrimary's 700, since the system has no bold body-text role. Update 2026-10-24 (explicit request): the overlay cell runs top to bottom of the row with the button centred, so on a block of two lines the fill no longer stops at one line; a heading after other blocks gets spacing-6 above it as a top border in the row's resting fill (bg.surface), so sections read as groups, the gap reads as blank surface whatever is behind the list, and the hover fill and overlay actions stay the size of the text; data-clickable marks a row whose whole box is the click target (pointer cursor), the click itself being the host's, as table-row's data-href. Update 2026-10-24 (explicit request): an included block answers hover and focus one step warmer, base.warm-200 (#EBE4D6, a new primitive, not from Figma) over its resting warm-100, in light; dark keeps bg.surface-pressed for both until it has a value of its own.
a11y_notes: Rows are <li> inside a <ul class="ds-block-list">; give the list an aria-label. Actions are real buttons; the drag handle is a plain element with a labelled icon (drag and drop has no keyboard equivalent here, the host page must offer one if it matters).

name: context-menu
description: The menu a right click opens on an element: a panel of actions at the pointer, built from dropdown-menu's own panel, items and divider. The host element carries data-context-menu="<menu id>"; choosing an item dispatches ds-context-menu-select on it.

props.name: id
props.description: The menu's id; a host element points at it with data-context-menu. One menu can serve every element of a list.

props.name: items
props.description: A list of { value, label, disabled } or { divider: true }. value comes back in ds-context-menu-select; a disabled item stays listed and takes no click.

props.name: label
props.description: The menu's accessible name (aria-label).

props.name: open
props.description: Rendered visible. Only for the demo; in use component.js shows and hides the menu.

props.name: inline
props.description: Variant inline: drawn in the flow instead of fixed at the pointer. Only for the demo and docs.

rationale: Requested by the maintainer (2026-10-19) for the CV sets sidebar (Delete, Rename, Duplicate, Download PDF), to be used on every list later. No design source defines a context menu, so nothing is invented: the panel is dropdown-menu's (white, 1px border in input-border-hover, no shadow, 44px items, base/100 hover, hairline divider, disabled state), reached by the same classes, which is why it needs dropdown-menu/style.css beside it. This component adds only what a floating menu needs: position fixed at the pointer, clamped to the viewport; z-index 40, above the sidebar (30) and below popups; a 200px minimum width (spacing.9 x 5; dropdown-menu's 100% is its trigger's width, and there is no trigger); and data-context-open on the host, which keeps the row's hover fill while its menu is open so it is clear what a click acts on. component.js is the same shape as dropdown-menu's: closes on Escape, an outside press, Tab, scroll, resize and window blur; arrow, Home and End keys move between enabled items. It does not decide what an item does: a destructive one is confirmed by the host. A destructive item is set apart by a divider and carries no color of its own: no design source asks for one.
a11y_notes: role="menu" with role="menuitem" buttons. Opens from the keyboard with the Menu key or Shift+F10 on a focusable host, at the host's lower left. Focus moves to the first item on open and returns to where it was on a keyboard close. Escape closes. A pointer-only host (a div) is not focusable: give it tabindex if it must be reachable by keyboard.

name: correction-row
description: One proposed correction in a list (e.g. a word text recognition was unsure of): found text -> proposal, a meta line, and Ignore / Accept, or the outcome once decided.

props.name: found
props.description: The text as found. Plain text.

props.name: proposal
props.description: The proposed replacement. Plain text.

props.name: meta
props.description: Where it is and how sure (e.g. 'Line 4 · 61 % sure').

props.name: state
props.description: open (two actions) | accepted (success tag) | ignored (neutral tag).

props.name: ignore_label
props.description: Secondary action label.

props.name: accept_label
props.description: Primary action label.

props.name: accepted_label
props.description: Tag text once accepted.

props.name: ignored_label
props.description: Tag text once ignored.

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Raw attributes on the Accept button (page-author markup only).

props.name: ignore_extra_attrs
props.description: Raw attributes on the Ignore button (page-author markup only).

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node. Reads as 'this -> that': the found text is struck through in text-subactive (it is being replaced, it is not the reader's mistake, so not the error color), the proposal in body-text-medium so the eye lands on what will stay. The meta line uses the data role like table metadata. The decision sits at the row's end, as the system's row actions do (table-cell's action cells are right-aligned): Ignore secondary, Accept primary, both dotted because they act within the view. Once decided, a passive tag (success for accepted, neutral for ignored) replaces the buttons so the list shows what is left to do. 45px min-height is the canvas's row height; a border-table hairline separates rows like table rows. Rows wrap at narrow widths. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: The arrow is aria-hidden; the row reads 'found, proposal, meta, Ignore, Accept'. Actions are real buttons (text-button).

name: disclosure
description: A section the reader opens and closes: a summary row with a chevron, a title and a passive caption, and a body. Native details element, no script.

props.name: title
props.description: The summary text.

props.name: caption
props.description: Passive text beside the title, for example a count.

props.name: open
props.description: Render the section open.

props.name: content
props.description: Plain text body (used when `items` is not given).

props.name: items
props.description: Optional list of strings, each rendered as its own paragraph in the body; replaces `content`.

rationale: Long pages of secondary content (examples, past mistakes) stay scannable when each part can be folded to one row. The native details and summary elements already give the toggle, the keyboard handling (Enter, Space) and the open state to assistive technology, so the component adds no script. The row shows state twice, by the chevron's turn and by the platform's own open state; the caption carries a count in the passive text color so the title stays the main thing. The chevron is the system's arrow-down icon used as a mask in currentColor, rotated a quarter turn when closed. A hairline under the section follows the other lists. Focus uses the accent outline of the system's other focusable text. No Figma node: taken from the application's design canvas of 2026-10-21.
a11y_notes: Native <details>/<summary>: the summary is a focusable button with expanded state, toggled by Enter and Space. The chevron is aria-hidden. Visible focus ring on the summary. Content inside a closed section is not rendered, so it is skipped by assistive technology until opened.

name: divider
description: A single 1px rule for separating two stacked sections (horizontal, Penpot's own instance) or two items in a row, e.g. grouped buttons in a table-header-actions bar (vertical, not from Penpot).

props.name: orientation
props.description: "horizontal" (default, Penpot's instance) renders a full-width, 1px, text-subactive rule for separating stacked sections. "vertical" (not sourced from Penpot) renders a small object-dark-passive square dot (spacing-1 x spacing-1), centered on its cross axis, for separating items within a horizontal row -- e.g. grouping buttons in a table-header-actions bar.

rationale: Penpot's "Divider" is a single main instance with one child rectangle, horizontal only; renamed to lowercase to satisfy the schema's name pattern. Horizontal: a full-width rule whose height is --ds-border-width-thin (1px) -- the border-width scale, because a hairline is a stroke, and spacing's smallest step (2px) would double its weight. Its fill is text.subactive, the token this system reserves for de-emphasized but visible content (table-cell's Source cell uses it for the same reason): enough contrast to read as a rule against bg.surface without competing with the text around it. No radius, no shadow: it is a flat rule. Vertical (not sourced from Penpot, which models only the horizontal instance): separates items within a horizontal row, e.g. grouped buttons in table-header-actions. It is a small square dot (spacing-1 x spacing-1), a design decision that replaced an earlier short vertical line, in object-dark.passive, the table border color, so it belongs to the same bordered vocabulary as the table around it; it is centered on the cross axis. Square, not round, because every radius token in the Base style resolves to 0 or 1px and a circle would be the one rounded shape in the system. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.

name: dropdown-menu
description: A floating menu of selectable action items, shown/hidden by a trigger element it's paired with (e.g. components/input-dropdown). Not a standalone widget — wrap a trigger and this menu together in a .ds-dropdown container to get real open/close/select behavior (see index.html). If the trigger uses input-dropdown's size="large" (100% width), mirror data-size="large" onto the .ds-dropdown wrapper too, so it switches to a block-level container the trigger can actually fill — see style.css.

props.name: items
props.description: Each item is a real .ds-dropdown-menu__item <button> child, not a JS-templated list — this component doesn't render from data, the consumer supplies the DOM. data-value on each item is read by component.js and included in the ds-dropdown-select event detail. An item of the form {'divider': true} renders a real divider/template.html <hr> instead of a button, grouping the items around it -- see rationale. With multiple=true an item may also carry selected (ticked) and mixed (the half-ticked box).

props.name: multiple
props.description: Checkbox items (explicit request 2026-10-01): the menu gets data-multiple and aria-multiselectable, each item a checkbox glyph before its label. A click toggles the item's aria-selected and keeps the menu open; ds-dropdown-select carries { value, label, selected, values }. The trigger's text is left alone.

props.name: scroll
props.description: Bounds the menu height (min of 320px and 45vh, override with --_menu-max-height) and scrolls the items inside it. For long lists such as a project picker in a popup.

rationale: Styled to Figma's opened dropdown (node 45:6594 of the application file), superseding the earlier Penpot values. The panel is bg.surface with a 1px border in the open trigger's base/750 (--ds-color-input-border-hover) and no shadow: the border is the edge, matching the trigger it belongs to. It sits 10px below the trigger (Figma's column gap, spacing-3 + spacing-1) and is exactly as wide as the trigger (border-box). Items are 44px rows with 10px padding, text on one line, touching edge to edge so the menu reads as one continuous surface; hover and keyboard focus fill bg.surface-pressed; the item matching the current value (aria-selected, kept by component.js) is Medium weight, so the current choice is visible without a checkmark. 10px and 44px have no spacing token and are composed from the scale (8+2, 40+4). A divider item composes the real divider component (declared in `uses`), drawn in object-dark.passive, the table rule color. A wrapper with data-size="large" or "compact" is block-level, so a full-width or 200px trigger can fill it. Not sourced from the design: open/close, positioning, outside-click and Escape to close, and aria-expanded toggling -- a static design tool doesn't model a floating layer, and without them this would be a picture of a menu. Items are in plain top-to-bottom DOM order, not the reversed authoring order of the Penpot instance, so the DOM order matches what is seen. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Multiple (explicit request 2026-10-01, no design source): each item shows the D_SYSTEM checkbox glyph (icons/checkbox, checkbox-selected, checkbox-semi-select) in table-cell's own checkbox colors, so a ticked item reads like a ticked row; all three glyphs are in the item and CSS shows the one for its state, as a row checkbox does. A ticked item keeps regular weight -- the box already says it is chosen. The menu stays open between clicks because ticking several values is the point. Opening (explicit request 2026-10-24): the menu fades in and slides down into place in 150ms ease-out each time it is shown, so it comes out of its trigger; closing is immediate; nothing moves under prefers-reduced-motion. Closing (explicit request 2026-10-24): the opening animation played back, 120ms ease-in, the menu fading and sliding 4px up into its trigger; component.js keeps it shown with data-closing until the animation ends (a timer catches a missed animationend), it takes no clicks meanwhile and counts as closed, and a reopen during it starts the opening over. Hidden at once under reduced motion.
a11y_notes: Menu container has role="listbox"; items have role="option". The trigger (paired via [data-dropdown-trigger] inside a .ds-dropdown wrapper) gets aria-expanded toggled automatically by component.js -- it must already carry aria-haspopup="listbox" itself (input-dropdown does). Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Clicking outside the .ds-dropdown wrapper closes it. Keyboard (2026-10-03): ArrowDown/ArrowUp on the closed trigger open the menu; in the open menu they move focus between enabled items (wrapping), Home/End jump to the first/last, Enter/Space pick the focused item (native button click), Tab closes the menu and lets focus move on. Opening from the keyboard focuses the selected item, else the first; closing while focus is inside the menu returns it to the trigger. Items stay ordinary Tab-reachable buttons rather than a roving tabindex, so nothing extra is needed for a menu a host builds at runtime. A divider item renders role="separator" (divider's own template), not role="option" -- it's not a selectable choice and carries no data-value, so component.js's select-click listener has nothing to attach to it in the first place. Multiple: the listbox has aria-multiselectable="true" and each option's aria-selected is its ticked state; the glyphs are aria-hidden.

name: dropzone
description: A file field that takes one file by drag and drop or the file picker, then shows that file as a row (thumbnail, name, size) with Remove. A real file input, so the form submits it without script.

props.name: id
props.description: The file input's id (the drop area is its <label>).

props.name: name
props.description: The file input's form name.

props.name: accept
props.description: The input's accept list (e.g. image/jpeg,image/png). A hint for the picker only; the server still checks the file.

props.name: required
props.description: The input is required.

props.name: prompt
props.description: Text before the choose link.

props.name: choose_label
props.description: The inline text-button-styled label that opens the picker.

props.name: hint
props.default: JPG or PNG, up to 20 MB
props.description: Formats and size limit, in the data role. '' renders none.

props.name: remove_label
props.description: Label of the file row's button.

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node. The dashed border-width-default edge in object-dark-passive is the drop-target sign (a solid edge would read as a panel); it and the add icon turn accent-1 while a file is dragged over, the only feedback a drag has. The fill is bg-surface-pressed: the canvas used the base-50 primitive, which has no themed token (it would stay light in the dark theme); flagged and replaced. The whole area is the input's <label>, so a click anywhere opens the picker and the input stays the single real control (keyboard focus shows the accent outline on the area). The choose text uses text-button's look (secondary, dotted: it stays on the page) without being a second button. Subdued texts use text-subactive (the canvas used the base-750 primitive, not themed). After a choice the area gives way to one file row so the reader sees what will be sent: thumbnail 64x84 (the canvas's size, a portrait page), name, size, pixel size, Remove. The thumbnail is a local object URL; nothing is uploaded by this component. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: The control is a native <input type=file> labelled by the whole area, so it is focusable and announced with the prompt text. Remove returns focus to the input. Drag and drop is an addition, never the only way.

name: empty-state
description: A standalone empty-state block: optional icon, message, optional action button. For non-table-row empty states (a paper-preview with nothing selected, a set table with no blocks yet) -- a table-row-shaped empty cell should keep using table-cell's own type="empty-state" instead.

props.name: message
props.description: The empty-state text. Reuses table-cell's own Penpot-sourced empty-state string/typography as the default.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon name (matches an icons/<name>.svg file), shown above the message.

props.name: action_label
props.description: Optional action button label (e.g. "Add project"). Composes a real text-button instance (secondary, dotted underline -- the action stays on the current view, it doesn't navigate). Omit for a message-only empty state.

props.name: size
props.description: "row": a 44px row for an empty table or block list (centered caption at half opacity, hairline under it).

rationale:
The design source has no standalone empty-state component. table-cell's type="empty-state" is sourced, but is shaped as one table-row cell (no icon or action slot), so it can't represent an empty preview, picker or pane. This component reuses table-cell's sourced message styling (bodyTextItalic, text.subactive) and adds only the layout a cell can't offer: a centered column with an optional icon above the message and an optional action (a real text-button, declared in `uses`) below it. The icon size (spacing-8, 32px) is a judgment call, not sourced: larger than inline spacing-7 glyphs because it heads a standalone block. The action is secondary / dotted because adding something from an empty state happens in place rather than navigating away.

Sizes, from the application's Figma screens:
- data-size="row": the empty row under a table head or block list. One table row high (spacing.row plus the hairline), the caption role (Inter Italic 16px) in text.active, the whole row including its hairline at 50% opacity; the hairline is base/150 in light and the pressed surface in dark.
- data-size="block": the empty area inside a picker. Fills its row, 40px above and below, caption role at half opacity, on the pressed surface (base/50 in light).
- data-size="text": one plain left-aligned line at half opacity on the surface color, inset spacing.cell, no height or hairline of its own.
- data-size="fill": the empty box of a preview pane. Absolutely positioned 20px inside its positioned parent, filled with base.175 (a palette token, the same in both themes), a hairline on its left edge, the message centered, the whole box at half opacity.
Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: The icon is aria-hidden: the message already carries the full meaning. The action is a real, focusable <button> from text-button's template, with no accessibility gap beyond what that component documents.

name: fade-in
description: What loads in fades in: elements inserted while a page is loading, and images when their pixels arrive, appear over 450ms instead of popping in. A utility class plus a small observer; no markup of its own.

props.name: content
props.default: Content that arrived after the page was drawn.
props.description: Template only: the text of the sample element. In use, the class .ds-fade-in goes on any element, or component.js adds it.

props.name: hold
props.description: data-fade-hold on an element in the page's HTML: it stays invisible and nothing inserted inside it fades on its own until dsFadeIn.settle() (or the 10s fail-safe); then it fades in once, as a whole.

props.name: region
props.description: data-fade-region on the area under the page's nav bar: dsFadeIn.leave(url) fades it out (200ms) before going to url.

rationale: A page that fills tables and sidebars from an API used to show a veil and hide everything until the data was in. Now nothing is hidden: the static page is drawn at once and each element that arrives fades in (opacity 0 to 1 with a 4px rise, 450ms ease-out, staggered 18ms per item up to 360ms). component.js watches insertions until the page calls dsFadeIn.settle() (or 10s pass), fades the topmost inserted element of each batch, and holds an image that is still downloading invisible until it has loaded, so a thumbnail fades in when it arrives, also after settle. After settle a re-render (sort, filter) is not animated: only what was loading fades. The fill mode is backwards, not both, so the finished fade leaves no stacking context behind. Not sourced from Figma (explicit request 2026-10-12, replacing the page-level loading state). Under prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Hold (explicit request 2026-10-24, "content appears once, with the animation"): on a page whose first view takes several requests (a list, then the item, then a preview), element-by-element fading showed the view in waves: skeletons, then each part as it arrived, then late pictures. A host marks its main area data-fade-hold; it is opacity 0, inner insertions are not animated, and settle() removes the attribute and fades the area in as one piece, so the host calls settle() when the last part is drawn. The fail-safe still releases it after 10s. Leave (explicit request 2026-10-24): navigating away fades the marked region out in 200ms, ease-in, faster than the 450ms appearance, so the page leaves as it came instead of being cut; forwards fill keeps it out until the next page paints, and a back-forward-cache restore clears it. Under prefers-reduced-motion it navigates at once. Update 2026-10-25: a picture with skeleton's placeholder (class ds-skeleton-image) is not held invisible: it shows its grey box while it loads and fades in by itself.
a11y_notes: Opacity and a 4px rise, 450ms; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Content stays in the accessibility tree while it fades.

name: figure
description: An image with its caption built in: the picture at its own proportions, full width of its container, and under it one grey italic line (who, where, when). Without a caption it is just the image; without an image it is a gray 16:9 placeholder.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. Omit it and the figure renders the gray 16:9 placeholder (data-empty).

props.name: alt
props.description: Text alternative of the image. Empty marks the image decorative, which is right when the caption already says what it shows.

props.name: caption
props.description: The line under the image. Omit it and no caption element is rendered.

rationale: Not drawn in Figma: the Portfolio preview needs a picture with a who / where / when line under it, and no existing component has a caption (paper-preview only has skeleton bars, gallery-image is a 160px thumbnail). Built on the semantic pair <figure> / <figcaption>, so the caption belongs to the image for assistive technology and for anyone reading the markup, with no wrapper logic. Every value is an existing token: the caption role (--ds-font-caption-*, Inter italic) in text-subactive, 4px (spacing-2) below the image, the object-dark-passive gray behind the image as in gallery-image, 16:9 for the empty state as in paper-preview's image placeholder. The image is never cropped (width 100%, height auto): portrait and landscape photos on one document sheet each keep their shape, which a fixed ratio with object-fit would not. Long unbroken captions wrap (overflow-wrap: anywhere) so a long place name cannot widen the sheet. Light and dark both come from the tokens; rendering verified in both themes.
a11y_notes: <figure>/<figcaption> ties the caption to the image. alt defaults to empty (decorative), because in the Portfolio the caption is the description; a host with no caption should pass a real alt. The caption color is text-subactive (black at 40% in light), which is below 4.5:1 on white: acceptable for supplementary credit lines, not for the only statement of anything important.

name: gallery
description: A horizontally-scrolling row (filmstrip/slider) of gallery-image thumbnails that functions as a real multi-select photo picker: click one (or several) to select it, each selected thumbnail shows its own selection-order badge (1st click = "1", 2nd = "2", ...), click again to deselect.
rationale:
Layout from Penpot's "Gallery" instance: a flex row, aligned start, column gap spacing-4 (12px), Token-bound. Penpot defines no overflow behavior (a fixed-width demo row with few images), so the row is a scrolling filmstrip (nowrap, overflow-x:auto, children flex-shrink:0), with spacing-3 (8px) padding top and bottom because overflow-x:auto also clips vertically, which would cut a selected image's outline. The demo holds 10 mixed-format images so the scroll is actually visible.

Selection (component.js, not sourced -- a static design tool doesn't model clicks): click to select, and each selected image shows a badge with its selection order; clicking again deselects and renumbers the rest so the order stays contiguous. The ordered selection is persisted to localStorage (key ds-gallery-selection:<gallery id>) and dispatched as ds-gallery-select, so another process or page can read it. The badge is accent-1, matching the selected image's outline, with a text-inverced numeral.

Scrollbar: the native one is hidden and replaced by a custom, always-visible bar in .ds-gallery-wrapper (outside the scrolling element, so it doesn't scroll away): a spacing-2 (4px) track in bg-surface-pressed with an accent-1 thumb sized to the visible fraction. It is interactive -- drag the thumb or click the track to scroll -- and grows to spacing-4 (12px) on hover and drag so it's easier to grab. It is absolutely positioned inside padding the wrapper reserves for the grown state, so growing never shifts layout. The row itself can be dragged to scroll with mouse or pen (touch already scrolls natively); a 4px threshold tells a drag from a click, and a drag never also toggles the image it ends on. Pointer capture is taken only once a drag is confirmed, because a captured pointer's click is delivered to the capturing element, which would stop plain clicks from reaching the images.

Reset: any element with data-gallery-reset="<gallery id>" clears that gallery's selection through the same path a click uses, via a ds-gallery-reset event, so a host (e.g. popup's gallery body) needs no gallery-specific code. The trigger is a two-step confirm: the first click arms it (label "Yes, reset selection", text-button's error status), the second resets and restores the original label and status; a click anywhere else while armed disarms it, the same outside-click mechanism dropdown-menu uses.

.ds-gallery-picker is a separate, plain scrolling row for gallery-image type="picker" cards: 10px gaps, native thin scrollbar, no custom scrollbar or drag-to-scroll. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: No list or grid role is added (Penpot's source has no such structure). Each composed gallery-image is a real control: role="button", tabindex="0", aria-pressed reflecting selection, Enter/Space toggle like a click. Placeholder images have no accessible name beyond the role; a host with real photos should add an aria-label per image. The scrollbar thumb has role="scrollbar", aria-orientation="horizontal", aria-controls pointing at the row, aria-valuenow/min/max as a 0-100 percentage, and tabindex="0" with ArrowLeft/Right (80% of the visible width) and Home/End -- needed because a native scroll container only answers arrow keys when it has focus itself. Drag-to-scroll has no keyboard equivalent of its own; the thumb and each image's Tab order cover the same range. Known gap: the reset trigger's armed state is not announced proactively (no live region); the button's accessible name does update, so re-reading it reveals the state.

name: gallery-image
description: One item of a gallery. type="image" (default): a thumbnail standing in for a photo, with an optional badge marking selection order. type="picker": a selectable 160px square card with an optional real image. type="text-icon": a text skeleton placeholder -- a bold label above a stack of gray bars, the last one shorter, in short / middle / full lengths -- selectable as a radio group with its text-icon siblings.

props.name: type
props.description: Sets data-type. "image" (default, attribute omitted in markup) renders the photo-thumbnail look, sized by the format prop below. "text-icon" renders the skeleton/placeholder look instead (120px fixed height, flexible width -- see rationale; format is not applicable in that case, Penpot only samples Text-icon at Format=landscape). Kebab-cased from Penpot's own Type axis (Image/Text-icon).

props.name: format
props.description: Only applies when type="image". Sets data-format, controlling width at a fixed 160px height: landscape (260px, wider), portrait (130px, narrower), square (160px, equal). Kebab-cased from Penpot's own Format axis (landscape/Portrait/Square).

props.name: selected
props.description: Sets data-selected, which every type renders as the same outline frame (see rationale). For type="image" the host also renders the .ds-gallery-image__badge child with the selection's order number (this component doesn't generate it). For type="text-icon" this only sets the initial state -- component.js wires single-select radio semantics across each group of text-icon siblings, so at most one card per group ends up selected at runtime.

props.name: subtype
props.description: Only applies when type="text-icon": short / middle / full, matching Penpot's Subtype axis. It determines how many .ds-gallery-image__bar children the template renders (1 full-width + 1 short for short, 2+1 for middle, 4+1 for full) and the label text.

props.name: src
props.description: Only applies when type="picker": URL of the picture, rendered as an (object-fit: cover, loading=lazy) over the placeholder fill. Omit for the placeholder. A failed load is hidden by component.js so the fill shows.

props.name: alt
props.description: Only applies with src: the 's alt text. Empty by default because the picker

rationale: type="image": sizes from Penpot's "Image" instances, all three formats sampled -- height 160px, width 260 / 130 / 160px for landscape / portrait / square (pixel-matched). The fill is a flat object-dark-passive gray standing in for a photo, as Penpot's own instances do (a flat-color rectangle, no image asset); a host sets a real background-image. Penpot's #ADADAD matches several tokens; object-dark-passive was chosen as the neutral, non-state fill. The selection badge (Penpot State="Selected") is a small square flush in the bottom-right corner: a text-inverced numeral in typography.heading5 on accent-1, the same color as the selected frame. Penpot's "Number-label" is a filled square with a text character, so it is HTML text, not an icon. The number and which images are selected are host state (gallery supplies them). Selected frame (all types): a 1px accent-1 outline. Hover (all types): a 1px text-active outline, no fill -- one shared affordance for both types. Outlines, not borders, so the pixel-matched sizes don't grow; hover is declared before selected so a hovered selected item keeps its accent outline. type="text-icon" (Penpot Subtype short / middle / full, purpose confirmed from Penpot's variants and exports): a skeleton placeholder -- the subtype's name as a bold label above flat gray bars standing in for lines of text, ending in one shorter 80px bar (short = 1+1 bars, middle = 2+1, full = 4+1). Boards are 120px high with spacing-6 (20px) padding; bar height and gaps are documented in style.css, including Penpot's visible overflow for middle and full. Width is not Penpot's 566px: the cards sit side by side and share their container (flex 1 1 0, min-width 0). Selection works as a radio group (component.js): siblings sharing a parent form one group, one selected at a time, with roving tabindex and arrow keys like native radios. type="picker": a selectable 160px square
a11y_notes: type="image" on its own is a static thumbnail; composed in gallery, gallery's component.js makes it a real toggle (role="button", tabindex, aria-pressed). A host with real photos should add an accessible label per image. type="picker" is a native <button> with aria-pressed. type="text-icon": the shared parent gets role="radiogroup", each card role="radio" with aria-checked, and a roving tabindex, so the group is one Tab stop; arrow keys move focus and selection together, Enter/Space select -- native radio behavior. Note: text-icon's real purpose is a loading skeleton, and a selectable skeleton isn't a real UI pattern; the selection exists to demonstrate the shared selected frame. Used purely as a loading state, wire no selection and mark the surrounding container role="status" / aria-busy instead.

name: header-block
description: The full header of a table: a title/tabs region (table-header) and an action-button cluster (table-header-actions), with an optional search, forming one header bar whose border-bottom separates it from the table's rows below.

props.name: size
props.description: big or small. Maps to Penpot's Size variant axis; controls the header's own padding scale (spacing.6/spacing.5 vs spacing.0/spacing.3). Does not affect table-header or table-header-actions content.

props.name: search
props.description: When true, renders a center search zone (composing input) between table-header and table-header-actions. Not a Penpot-sourced axis -- see rationale.

props.name: search_placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the search input, only rendered when search=true.

props.name: layout
props.description: bulk: the bulk-actions row over a table -- table-header-actions flush left (the actions act on selected rows; give them status 'disabled' until something is selected), plus, with search=true, an always-open search docked right. No table-header.

props.name: more_actions
props.description: layout='bulk' only: a second table-header-actions group, same item shape as actions, right after the first and set apart by divider's vertical dot (explicit request 2026-10-01: page-wide actions, then the selected rows' bulk actions).

props.name: search_plain
props.description: layout='bulk' with search=true: the field keeps input's own unboxed rest state (no border at rest) instead of header-block's boxed-at-rest search; input's hover and focus states as ever.

rationale:
Only Size is modeled as a variant. Penpot's other axis, Type (Archived / Found / Analysed / Queue / Queue-Small), changes only which title table-header renders and how many actions table-header-actions renders -- those components' own variants -- so modeling it here would duplicate their variant surfaces in a shell with no visual opinion about them.

data-size="big" (Figma header row): a plain 60px bg.surface row with 20px side padding, no gap between actions, no frame and no top padding, and one hairline under it -- the same hairline every table row has, so the header reads as the table's first row. data-size="small" keeps the earlier shaded bar: bg.surface-pressed with the border-width-thin / object-dark-passive border of table-cell's grid, inner padding spacing.3 (8px, Token-bound in Penpot's Queue/Small instance). Nested table-header's own chip background and border are reset inside the row so the two don't form a doubled box. The row is justify-content: space-between, which docks the title left and the actions right regardless of either's width. The divider Penpot draws under the header is not composed: the row's own border-bottom does that job, and a text.subactive divider against it would render as a doubled, two-tone line.

Search (not sourced from Penpot): one search box per table, filtering its rows. It composes input's template unchanged (no icon; the icon set has no search glyph). With a search, the row switches from space-between to flex-start + gap, because space-between only works for exactly two children. By default a "Search" trigger reveals the input and blurring an empty input collapses it back, so an unused field doesn't take header space; a non-empty input stays open. data-open="always" renders the input with no trigger, and data-align="end" docks the zone to the right edge. layout="bulk" is the bulk-actions row: table-header-actions flush left, an optional always-open search right, no title. The search field keeps a visible border through header-block's own rule, although input's transparent fill is borderless at rest. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. more_actions (bulk layout, explicit request 2026-10-01): a second action group after the first, set apart by divider's vertical dot -- the same dot this system already uses between actions -- so page-wide actions (Add, Fetch) and actions on the selected rows read as two groups in one reading line. search_plain: the field is input's own, unboxed at rest, for a header whose search shouldn't stand out as a box. 2026-10-23: the big row uses min-height and wraps its groups (actions, search) onto more rows on a narrow window instead of widening the page.
a11y_notes: The search input is input's plain native field; labeling is the host page's responsibility, as input documents. The search trigger and the input both stay in the DOM and component.js only flips which is visible (data-open) -- a show/hide of the same kind as popup and dropdown-menu.

name: header-tab
description: One panel in a full-width row of N equal-width section tabs (e.g. a For Review / Analysed / Archived / Filtered strip) -- each tab is its own flex:1 box with a background and border that change with selection, tiling edge to edge across the row. Distinct from table-header's type="2-tabs" (a single content-hugging chip holding both labels); see rationale. The host composes N instances inside a shared role="tablist" wrapper and typically renders a header-block bar below the strip for the active tab's own search and bulk actions.

props.name: active
props.description: Whether this tab is the current section. Sets aria-selected and switches background/text color/underline per rationale.

props.name: label
props.description: The tab's title text (e.g. "For Review").

props.name: count
props.description: Optional secondary caption rendered beside the label (e.g. "4 total, 5 submitted"). Omitted entirely from the DOM when not passed, matching table-header's own optional info caption.

props.name: size
props.description: "compact": 56px tabs for a pane head (see rationale); default is the 60px full-width strip.

props.name: href
props.description: Render the tab as an <a href> (through safe_url) so it navigates, e.g. between pages, instead of a button that switches a panel. Keeps role="tab" and aria-selected.

rationale:
Read from the application's Figma file: the repeated "header" instance used identically across its section screens (nodes 150:16076 active / 150:16077 inactive), with only the active assignment changing. Height is a fixed 60px, the same as the nav bar it sits flush beneath; padding is Figma's 10px vertical / 20px horizontal. The label and count sit in an inner .ds-header-tab__text wrapper with Figma's bottom alignment and 10px gap, while the outer tab centers that block vertically -- Figma's own two-level structure.

Colors read off Figma's two states: active = bg.surface + text.active label; inactive = bg.surface-pressed + text.subactive label, the same active/inactive vocabulary table-header's 2-tabs uses. The count uses text.subactive in both states (Figma's 50% caption). Figma's 0.5px bottom border is drawn with border-width-thin in border-table, the token every table line uses, so lines match across pages in both themes, rather than a 0.5px-only token. The inactive label carries Figma's permanent dotted underline: it stays in the view when clicked (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions).

Why not an extension of table-header's 2-tabs: that variant is one content-hugging chip holding both labels, sitting beside table-header-actions; here each tab independently stretches flex:1 across the whole row, carries its own background and border, and the strip sits above a separate header bar. None of 2-tabs' CSS transfers. Figma's "actions-block" child holds one invisible, unpopulated placeholder button on every instance and is not modeled.

data-size="compact" is a pane-head tab (Figma node 150:16299): 56px tall, 20px side padding, a hairline on the left of every tab (the divider between panes), the label in the "title" role, the count in the caption role and hidden while the tab is open. .ds-header-tabs holds tabs as a flex row. Not sourced from Figma: click-to-switch in component.js, scoped to the nearest role="tablist" ancestor because each tab is composed independently by the host; a tab row that never switches would be a dead affordance. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: A real role="tab" <button>, per the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern. The host wraps the tabs in a role="tablist" container (this component doesn't own that wrapper) and pairs each tab with its role="tabpanel". aria-selected reflects the active prop and is kept in sync on click by component.js. The focus-visible outline (accent-1, 2px, matching table-header's tabs) has no Figma equivalent: static design tools don't model keyboard focus. With href the tab is an <a role="tab">: the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern expects tabs to switch panels in place, so use href only when each tab is a separate page and mark the current one with active.

name: image-regions
description: A photo (or a page placeholder) with rectangles over the parts that need the reader's eye, e.g. where text recognition was unsure (uncertain) or where a correction was taken (accepted).

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL (through safe_url). None: the page placeholder.

props.name: alt
props.description: The image's alt text.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the placeholder.

props.name: regions
props.description: List of {x, y, w, h, kind, label}: position and size in percent of the image, kind uncertain | accepted, label an accessible description (none: decorative).

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node. The rectangles use the same signal pairs as inline-mark's states in the text beside the photo (uncertain: the for-review row-status edge and fill; accepted: the approved row-status edge, no fill, so the text under it stays readable; both themed, unlike the signal-* primitives), so photo and text point at each other. Edge width border-width-default so the frame reads at a glance over a busy photo. The placeholder (grey lines on bg-surface-pressed, 440px high -- the canvas's portrait page) stands in while no image is shown; the canvas used the base-50 primitive, which has no themed token, replaced by bg-surface-pressed. Positions are host data in data-* attributes, applied as private custom properties by component.js, so no style value comes from the host. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: With an image, alt describes it; without, the frame is role=img with label. Each labelled region is role=img with its own name; unlabelled regions are aria-hidden.

name: inline-mark
description: A run of text inside a sentence that marks a correction: struck-through text to remove, or filled text to add, with an optional tooltip.

props.name: kind
props.description: remove (struck through, system-error-strong), add (signal-success-light fill, success-strong text, medium weight, dotted underline) or uncertain (row-status-for-review fill and outline: text a recognizer was unsure of).

props.name: text
props.description: The run's text. Plain text.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Optional explanation; set as data-tooltip, so the tooltip component shows it on hover and focus. Makes the mark focusable (tabindex 0).

props.name: href
props.description: Optional link target: the mark renders as <a> (keeps its kind's look, pointer, thin outline on hover), e.g. to the explanation of this correction.

props.name: current
props.description: The mark whose explanation is open: outlined in its own color (data-current, aria-current on a link).

rationale: Shows a correction in the sentence itself, so a learner sees what changed and where. Two kinds: remove is struck through in the error color; add has a light success fill, the strong success color, medium weight and a dotted underline, so it is distinguishable without color (a struck-through run versus an underlined one). Colors are existing tokens (system-error-strong follows the theme; the signal pair is the palette's own light/strong, like the tag, so the add fill keeps its contrast in both themes). The mark inherits the surrounding font and size and only changes weight for add, so it can sit in any line of text. The tooltip is the existing data-tooltip mechanism; a marked run with a tooltip is focusable so it is reachable by keyboard. No source in Figma: drawn from the application's design canvas of 2026-10-21; no Figma node exists. uncertain (2026-10-23): the for-review row-status pair as fill and outline (themed; the signal-warning primitives stay light under light text in the dark theme) marks text the reader should check (text recognition was unsure); told apart from the corrections by shape (an outline, no underline, no strike), not color alone.
a11y_notes: Plain inline span. Strike-through and fill are visual only: a screen reader reads the text without saying it was removed or added, so a host should state the change in text nearby (for example a visually hidden 'removed' / 'added', or the corrected sentence in full). The tooltip text is only reachable by hover and focus.

name: input
description: A single-line text field for entering short freeform text. Use for names, search terms, notes — anything that isn't a fixed set of choices (use input-dropdown for that).

props.name: type
props.description: "text" (default, a single-line <input>), "password" (a single-line <input type="password">) or "textarea" (a multi-line <textarea>, not from Penpot -- see rationale).

props.name: fill
props.description: "transparent" (default) or "filled" (base/250 fill). Figma's Input property is literally named Size, but its two values are fills; it is exposed as fill so it cannot be confused with input-dropdown's width `size`. Sets data-fill. Hover fills either one.

props.name: value
props.description: Current text content. Maps to Penpot's Filled state when non-empty.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when empty, drawn as body text at 50% opacity (Figma). Typed text is full opacity.

props.name: rows
props.description: Only meaningful when type="textarea". Sets the native rows attribute. When given, it sets data-rows and the lines decide the height (no 160px minimum).

props.name: name
props.description: Native name attribute, so the field is submitted with its form.

props.name: id
props.description: Native id attribute, for a visible <label for>.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name (aria-label) for a field without a visible <label>.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Native disabled attribute. Not a Figma state; the browser's disabled styling applies.

props.name: required
props.description: Native required attribute.

props.name: autocomplete
props.description: Native autocomplete token, e.g. "username" or "current-password".

rationale: Styled to Figma's Input (node 33:8199 of the application file): a 40px box with a 1px base/400 border and 10px padding, no shadows. Figma's Size property (transparent | filled) is exposed as `fill`. Hover fills the field (base/250) and darkens the border (base/750); focus is a white fill with an accent border, typed text at full opacity. Figma has exactly three states (default, hover, focused) and no disabled, error or pressed state, so none is styled. State is native CSS (:hover, :focus, ::placeholder), no `state` prop. Colors come from the input tokens (--ds-color-input-fill, -border, -border-hover, -border-focus), defined in both themes. The transparent fill has no visible border at rest (Figma D_SYSTEM Inputs card, node 103:4758): the field sits inside something that already frames it, and shows its border on hover and focus, matching input-dropdown; table-cell's notes cell and header-block's search restore the boxed look in their own CSS. width:100% rather than Figma's 280px: that is the swatch's frame, not a component constraint. Not sourced from Figma: type="textarea", which reuses the same box rules without the fixed height. Replaces an earlier Penpot version; its Penpot `source` is kept for traceability. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Native <input type="text">, so labeling is the host page's responsibility (a <label> or aria-label). Focus is shown by the fill turning white and the border turning the accent color (Figma draws no separate outline). The placeholder is 50% opacity body text and is not a substitute for a label.

name: input-dropdown
description: A select-style field: shows the current choice with a dropdown affordance arrow, opens components/dropdown-menu when activated (composed, see index.html — wrap this trigger and a .ds-dropdown-menu together in a .ds-dropdown container). Renamed from Penpot's literal component name "Input_with-icon" — its content is a 'Dropdown' text label plus a chevron, i.e. a select trigger, not a text input with a decorative leading icon.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value shown in the field.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Set when `value` is only a prompt ("Select option"), not a real choice: the label is drawn at 50% opacity like Figma's placeholder text. Sets data-placeholder; component.js removes it when the paired dropdown-menu selects an item.

props.name: fill
props.description: "transparent" (default) or "filled" (base/250 fill). Figma's Input property is named Size but its values are fills; exposed as fill so it stays distinct from the width `size` below. Sets data-fill. Hover fills either one.

props.name: size
props.description: small (140px), middle (300px), or large (100% — fills its container). Sets a fixed width via data-size; the field never grows/shrinks on its own. Not from Penpot — its demo instances were all a single fixed 160px, an artifact of that documentation swatch's own frame size, not a real size system. These three values and their pixel widths were specified directly by the user rather than derived from Penpot (middle started at 240px, widened +60px to 300px on later user request). compact is 200px (a pane head's source dropdown).

rationale: Styled to Figma's Input, Type=text+icon (node 33:8199 of the application file): the same 40px box as `input` (1px base/400 border, 10px padding, no shadows) with the label and a 24px arrow 10px apart. Figma's Size property (transparent | filled) is exposed as `fill`. Hover fills the field (base/250) and darkens the border (base/750); Figma's focused variant (white fill, base/750 border, arrow pointing up) is applied for :focus-visible and for the open menu (aria-expanded), so the arrow shows which way the menu is. Colors come from the input tokens (--ds-color-input-*, plus --ds-color-input-icon for the base/600 arrow). The label is 50% opacity while it is only a prompt and full opacity once a choice is made, so `placeholder` (data-placeholder) is opt-in; component.js clears it on the paired dropdown-menu's ds-dropdown-select event. Renamed from Penpot's "Input_with-icon" because its content is a label plus a chevron, i.e. a select trigger, and the schema's name pattern calls for kebab-case describing behavior. The arrow reuses icons/arrow-down.svg. Figma has only default, hover and focused states, so no disabled or error state is styled. size (small / middle / large) is a fixed-width system not traceable to the design source; data-size="compact" is 200px wide, for a dropdown in a pane head (Figma node 150:16284) -- mirror it onto the .ds-dropdown wrapper so the trigger fills it (see dropdown-menu). Replaces an earlier Penpot version; its `source` is kept for traceability. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Renders as a native <button> (not a real <select>). aria-haspopup="listbox" is set so assistive tech announces it opens a choice list; aria-expanded is toggled automatically by components/dropdown-menu/component.js when this trigger is wrapped in a .ds-dropdown alongside a .ds-dropdown-menu (see index.html). It also still dispatches ds-input-dropdown-open on click/Enter/Space (free via <button>) independent of whether a real menu is attached, for a host page that wants to wire up its own menu instead.

name: loading-veil
description: A dim veil over one area with a small dark "Loading" tooltip: the area under it is loading. Show and hide with the hidden attribute.

props.name: label
props.description: Tooltip text.

props.name: variant
props.description: "bare" (2026-10-25): only the spinner, twice the size, centred in the area, no veil and no box; the label is for screen readers only. Omitted: the veil with its Loading tooltip.

rationale: The veil covers its positioned parent (inset 0) above the content (z-index 5, below popups at 100 and toasts at 200) with the popup overlay color (bg.overlay) at 50% opacity, exactly like a popup's backdrop, so 'this area is busy' reads the same way as 'this area is behind a dialog'. The tooltip is a dark box (Figma base/900 with a base/1000 hairline, white text, 10px padding and gap) holding the spinner glyph (a CSS mask, so it takes the text color) and the label. It is centered horizontally and translated -50% / -50%, so the host places its center by setting style.top (Figma draws it at the middle of the window, not of the area). Not sourced from Figma: the hidden-attribute API and role="status". Rendering verified in light and dark themes. The spinner rotates clockwise, 1.2s linear per turn, and stops under prefers-reduced-motion. Bare (explicit request 2026-10-25): an area that is still being filled (a page or a preview on its way in) shows only the spinner at its centre, with no veil (nothing in it is blocked) and no box; the glyph is twice the size in the passive dark color, and it does not take pointer events. Update 2026-10-25 (explicit request): the spinner is an ordinary one, a faint ring with a quarter arc in full ink (icons/loading.svg), instead of the half-filled circle. The bare spinner is drawn in accent-1 (explicit request 2026-10-25); the boxed one stays white on its dark tooltip. Later the same day (explicit request): the arc has square ends, the ring is grey (object-dark-passive) and the arc accent; drawn in CSS to the icon's geometry, since a mask paints one color.
a11y_notes: role="status" so the loading message is announced when the veil is shown; the spinner is aria-hidden. The veil does not trap focus: the host should also mark the area inert while loading if it must not be used.

name: message
description: One turn of a task and answer exchange: a filled prompt panel or an outlined, right-aligned answer, with an optional label, an optional note line and optional inline corrections.

props.name: variant
props.description: prompt (filled bg-surface-pressed panel), answer (outlined, right-aligned) or task (inverted: text-active fill, bg-surface text, the text in title type (body size, bold)). Other values fall back to prompt.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional small uppercase caption above the text.

props.name: text
props.description: The message text. Plain text.

props.name: segments
props.description: Optional list of {text, kind?, tooltip?, href?, current?} replacing `text`. A segment with kind remove or add renders as an inline-mark (with its tooltip); others are plain text.

props.name: note
props.description: Optional plain text under the text, in text-subactive (e.g. the instruction that goes with a question).

props.name: note_tooltip
props.description: Optional tooltip text (newlines start new lines) shown by a "(more)" trigger at the end of the note: dotted underline, focusable. The note's own text stays plain.

props.name: note_more
props.description: Label of the note's tooltip trigger (in brackets after the note).

rationale: A task and the learner's reply are two voices, so they differ by shape, not only by color: the prompt is a filled panel (bg-surface-pressed), the answer is outlined with the hairline token and aligned to the right. Padding is spacing-5 for both; the text uses the body type, the label the data role in uppercase and text-subactive, so the label reads as a caption. Segments let the same box show a corrected sentence by composing inline-mark; the plain-text path covers every other case. Arrangement of messages in a column (gaps, a pinned input) is the host's layout, not part of this component. No Figma node: taken from the application's design canvas of 2026-10-21. The optional note is a second line under the text in the body type and text-subactive: a question and the instruction that goes with it are one turn, and the color alone ranks them without a new type style. The task variant opens a turn: inversion and the title type (the body size, bold) make the question the first thing read, ahead of the answer and the feedback under it, without a new color.
a11y_notes: Plain divs of text; no role. A host that shows a conversation should put the messages in a list or a log region and say who speaks (the label can carry it). Corrections come from inline-mark; see its notes on conveying removed and added text to assistive technology.

name: nav-bar
description: The primary top navigation bar: a workspace switcher (left), the page / section links (center), and a theme toggle (right). A composition shell, like table-row -- it composes real input-dropdown and text-button instances rather than restyling them. It stays pinned to the top of the viewport while the page scrolls (position:sticky, top:0), with an opaque background and a bottom hairline so it stays legible over scrolling content; this is part of the component, so every page that uses it gets the same behavior.

props.name: nav_links
props.description: Center links: {label, href, current}.

props.name: workspace_label
props.description: Value of the left dropdown.

props.name: right_actions
props.description: Extra actions before the theme toggle: {label, href} is a link; {label, form_action, hidden} is a POST form around a submit button (hidden: name -> value, e.g. a CSRF token).

rationale:
Layout from Penpot's Nav-bar instance: a flex row, centered, justify-content: space-between; both side slots are flex rows too, so buttons of different heights line up. Box values follow the Figma nav instance: 10px (spacing-cell) padding on all four sides and a 0.5px bottom hairline in object-dark-passive -- raw 0.5px because Figma draws it and --ds-border-width-thin (1px) stays correct for tables. Penpot's column gap of 101px is not reproduced: it is an artifact of a fixed 1240px demo board, and with space-between any explicit gap would be right at exactly one width. Sticky, not fixed: the bar is always the page's first full-width element, so both look the same once scrolled, but sticky keeps it in document flow and content below needs no hand-maintained offset. bg.surface and the hairline keep it legible over content scrolling beneath it.

Left: a composed input-dropdown at 160px (the width table-cell's dropdown cell uses for the same Penpot source). Center: text-buttons with no gap (Penpot's gap is 0; the buttons' own padding separates them). Which link is primary (current page) is markup the host supplies; Penpot's "Property 1" axis only changes which link carries it, so it isn't a style variant. Right: the theme toggle is a real text-button (secondary, active, dotted -- toggling stays on the page) with an icon and a visible label ("Dark" / "Light"); both name the target theme, the same convention the site's own toggle uses. The label is not sourced from Penpot, whose theme icon is a bare glyph. The theme icons draw a 16-unit circle in a 24-unit viewBox, so a spacing-7 (24px) box reproduces Penpot's 16px glyph. .ds-nav-bar__theme-* classes are kept only as stable selectors for the toggle script and carry no CSS.

Notification dot: .ds-nav-bar__dot inside a nav link is a 12px accent-2 circle at the link's right edge, toggled with hidden -- an unread-updates marker. It is the only round shape in the system; Figma draws it round. Keeping it in sync across pages is the host's concern. Not sourced from the design: the link click-swap and the theme toggle's behavior, without which the current link would never change and the toggle wouldn't toggle. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Additions 2026-10-23: right_actions for actions such as signing out (a POST form whose box is display: contents so it does not change the row); the bar wraps its groups onto more rows on a narrow window instead of widening the page, and has z-index 3 (pane's sticky head's value) so positioned content scrolling under the sticky bar does not paint over it. 2026-10-23: the left and right groups take equal shares of the remaining width (flex 1 1 0, never below their content), so the center links sit at the bar's true middle, aligned with a page's centered content, instead of midway between two groups of different widths.
a11y_notes: A real <nav aria-label="Primary"> landmark (not in Penpot; a design tool has no landmarks). Center links are <button> elements with aria-current="page" on the current one, updated on click by component.js; in a real site they should be <a href>. The theme toggle's accessible name is its visible label ("Dark" / "Light"), with the icon aria-hidden and no separate aria-label, so visible and accessible names can't diverge (WCAG 2.5.3); both update on every click to name what activating it does. The workspace switcher is input-dropdown as-is; see its notes.

name: note-item
description: One word noted while reading, in a side list: the word colored by gender, its translation, the form it had in the text, and either an 'in list' tag or an 'Add to list' action.

props.name: label
props.description: The word, with its article for nouns. Plain text.

props.name: article
props.description: der | die | das colors the word (der accent-1, die row-status-declined-text, das row-status-approved-text); anything else keeps the text color.

props.name: translation
props.description: The translation. Plain text.

props.name: form
props.description: The form the word had in the text, in the data role.

props.name: in_list
props.description: true: a passive neutral tag; false: the add action.

props.name: in_list_label
props.description: The tag's text.

props.name: add_label
props.description: The action's label (secondary, dotted).

props.name: submit
props.description: The add action submits its enclosing form.

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Raw attributes on the add button (page-author markup only).

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node. Three lines because the three facts are read in order: which word (in the same gender colors as table-cell's article links, so a noun's gender is visible before its article is read), what it means, how it appeared in the text (data role, text-subactive: context, not content). The state sits at the end of the first line: a passive tag when nothing is left to do, a secondary dotted text-button when there is (it stays in the view). Padding spacing-4 / spacing-6 matches a pane's content inset; a border-table hairline separates items like table rows. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Plain text lines and a real button; color is never the only carrier of the gender, which the article in label also states.

name: page-head
description: The 60px bar under the nav bar of a work page: the page's title and its main action on the left, secondary actions on the right, one hairline underneath.

props.name: title
props.description: Page title (an h1), cut with an ellipsis when it is too long.

props.name: main_action
props.description: Label of the text button next to the title.

props.name: editable
props.description: The title can be clicked to rename it: shows the text cursor and a dotted underline on hover and keyboard focus. The host swaps in the input on click; the component only styles the two states.

props.name: editing
props.description: Render the rename field (.ds-page-head__title-input) in place of the title. Same type tokens, no padding or border, so the bar does not change size.

props.name: actions_left
props.description: List of {label, href?, submit?, underline?} rendered as text buttons next to the title, replacing main_action. An empty list renders none. Unset: the single main_action button, as before.

props.name: actions_right
props.description: Same item shape, rendered on the right, replacing the fixed Undo / Download PDF buttons. An empty list renders none. Unset: those two buttons, as before.

props.name: meta_text
props.description: A passive line of text after the left-hand actions (counts, a note). Plain text, not interactive.

rationale: Height is spacing.9 + spacing.6 (60px), side padding spacing.6 (20px), bg.surface with one hairline (object-dark.passive) under it. The title is the heading-3 role (Inter 24px; one step above the heading-4 the Figma frames use, 2026-10-18, explicit request: the set name read too small) with line-height normal, so the bar's height, not the type scale, sets the rhythm. The gap between title and main action is spacing.cell (10px); the right group has no gap because text buttons hug their labels (see text-button). Both groups are flex rows with min-width 0, so a long title ellipsizes instead of pushing the actions out. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Rename in place (2026-10-11): the title is the heading-4 role; the rename field reuses the same four type tokens with zero padding, border and fill, so swapping title for field changes nothing about the box: no jump, no reflow of the actions. It is marked by an accent line drawn as an inset shadow (not a border, which would add height) and sized to its text with field-sizing: content, capped at the bar. The editable title carries the system's dotted-underline clickable affordance on hover and focus only, so a read-only title looks as before. Not from Figma (the Figma bar draws no editing state); built from existing tokens only. 2026-10-23: min-height instead of height and flex-wrap, so on a narrow window the groups wrap onto a second row instead of widening the page; at full width it is still 60px.
a11y_notes: The title is an h1. The buttons are real text-buttons; keyboard focus uses their own ring. An editable title is focusable (tabindex 0) and the host opens the field on Enter or F2 as well as click; the field has aria-label 'Set name'. Escape cancels and Enter or leaving the field commits, both owned by the host.

name: pane
description: One column of a two-column work area: a 56px head (title and caption at half opacity, optional action button) over a body that scrolls on its own. .ds-split lays panes side by side.

props.name: id
props.description: Prefix of the title's id, used by aria-labelledby.

props.name: title
props.description: Pane title.

props.name: caption
props.description: Caption next to the title (a count, a page count).

props.name: action
props.description: Label of the head's text button.

props.name: body_html
props.description: Block body set with {% set body_html %}...{% endset %} before the include (markup-safe; its own {{ }} autoescape). A plain string is escaped like content.

props.name: action_href
props.description: The head's action is a link (e.g. Close back to the view without this side pane).

props.name: no_action
props.description: No head action.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: The title at full opacity (data-emphasis).

props.name: data-motion
props.description: On .ds-pane, set by the host for one animation and removed on animationend: enter (slide in from the right edge + fade in, 220ms), leave (slide out + fade out, 160ms, surface fill), fade-in / fade-out (the same without the slide, for a pane stacked above its list). No motion under prefers-reduced-motion.

rationale:
Head height is spacing.9 + spacing.5 (56px), side padding spacing.6, bg.surface, one hairline under it. The title uses the "title" role (Inter SemiBold 16px) and the caption the caption role (Inter Italic 16px), both at 50% opacity as in Figma, bottom-aligned so their baselines meet, spacing.cell apart. .ds-pane__body and .ds-pane__scroll are separate so a positioned body (e.g. one a loading-veil covers) can wrap the scrolling region, while a simple pane scrolls directly under the head. The scrollbar is hidden (scrollbar-width: none); wheel, keys and touch still scroll.

Attributes: data-divider="start" on the head and body draws a hairline on the pane's left edge (the divider between two panes); data-emphasis="true" on the title shows it at full opacity; a body with the hidden attribute is hidden (tab panels).

Resizable split: any flex row with data-resizable and a .ds-split__handle between two neighbours. The handle is a 0-wide flex item on the border between them, with an 8px (spacing.3) grab area centered on the line and a 2px accent line on hover, focus and while dragging. Dragging, or ArrowLeft / ArrowRight (24px a step), resizes the target: data-resize-target="end" (default) the element after the handle, "start" the one before it. data-min-size / data-min-rest set the target's and the rest's minimum in pixels (default 320 each). The size is applied as data-resized plus --_resize-size on the target, not an inline flex, so CSS states keep priority (sidebar-list's collapsed rule beats it, and the handle beside a collapsed sidebar is hidden). The size is not remembered across a reload (explicit request 2026-10-12): every split starts as the CSS has it, and data-resize-key only clears a share an earlier version stored. Within a session the size is a share of the row, so another window width keeps the proportion. It emits ds-split-resize and a window resize, so nested splits re-apply their stored share and paper-preview's scroll thumb updates. Not sourced from Figma: the handle and resizing; the design shows only the divider line. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Additions 2026-10-23: body_html gives the pane a block slot (tables, paragraphs, lists) instead of string content only; action_href makes the head action a link, dotted because closing a side pane stays on the same view; caption '' renders none. Motion, 2026-10-23: a side pane opening beside a list slides 24px (spacing-7) and fades in, and leaves the same way, so the eye follows where the content came from; only transform and opacity animate, because animating the list's column widths re-laid out every row on every frame (measured: dropped frames on a 100-row table, none with this). While leaving the pane takes bg-surface so a list already widened underneath does not show through. Functional motion, off under prefers-reduced-motion.
a11y_notes: The pane is a <section>; label it with aria-labelledby pointing at the title. The head button is a real text-button. The resize handle is role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical", focusable, with aria-valuenow/min/max as the end pane's share of the split in percent; give it an aria-label naming what it resizes.

name: paper-preview
description: A page preview shell for document-style cards (templates, collections), composed with skeleton placeholder content rather than real copy. Two modes: one-longread (a single continuous sheet, text placeholder only) and paged-preview (several A4 sheets stacked with gaps, scrollable inline, text and image placeholders). Each mode supports portrait and landscape.

props.name: mode
props.description: Sets data-mode. "one-longread" (default) renders a single continuous page with no gap/scroll behavior -- generalizes Penpot's real Template/Draft pattern (one board, no page split). "paged-preview" renders several .ds-paper-preview__page children stacked with an 8px gap inside a fixed-height, vertically-scrollable frame -- generalizes Penpot's real Collection/Template-Visual pattern (several Page-N boards in a flex column).

props.name: orientation
props.description: Sets data-orientation, which controls each sheet's aspect-ratio: "portrait" is 538:761, "landscape" 761:538 -- both true A4 (1:sqrt(2)), pixel-matched to Penpot's A4-proportioned Page-N boards and their transpose. The card stretches to 100% of its container's width; sheets scale with it.

rationale:
Generalizes the two structural patterns of Penpot's "Paper-Cards" board into a blank, reusable shell (Penpot has no paper-preview component): one-longread is a single uninterrupted sheet; paged-preview is several sheets in a column with a spacing.3 (8px) gap, Token-bound in Penpot and confirmed by measured positions. The container is bg.surface with no padding, so it shows only in the gaps between sheets. Sheets are true A4 (1:sqrt(2)): landscape 761:538, pixel-matched to Penpot's one A4-proportioned instance, portrait its transpose. Sheets are width:100% with aspect-ratio, so the proportion holds at any container width. In light, a sheet is white (Figma base/0); a picture inside a sheet fills its box (object-fit: cover). No shadow, border or radius: none of the sourced instances has any, so a flat rectangle is the actual sourced look.

paged-preview scrolls inline within a fixed max-height of 500px (a viewport constraint, not a token; vh would break inside the auto-resizing iframe the site embeds demos in). The native scrollbar is hidden and replaced by an overlay thumb, the same technique gallery uses horizontally: it shows only while scrolling and fades out after, and as an absolutely positioned overlay it never shifts content. Placeholder bars reuse gallery-image's skeleton convention (object-white.disabled bars, spacing-2 within a stack, spacing-6 between sections); the image placeholder reuses gallery-image's object-dark-passive stand-in at 16:9. .ds-paper-preview-stack is the scrolling column of sheets used inside a pane. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: A visual placeholder shell: the skeleton bars and rectangles stand in for content that doesn't exist yet, so they carry no role or label. A host rendering real document content into the sheets adds the real structure at that point (headings, landmarks, alt text). The scrollable frame is a plain overflow:auto <div> with no tabindex or role="region", since an empty region would be a false affordance; add both once real content is composed in. The custom scrollbar is aria-hidden and pointer-events:none -- a visual echo of native scrolling, not a control.

name: popup
