description: A modal panel: a title, a body (free text, a single input field, or a gallery + text-icon selector), and a bottom action row of one or two buttons, shown over a real full-viewport dimmed backdrop that a trigger button opens and the bottom row's own buttons (or Escape/backdrop click) close. No close/X control -- dismissal is via the bottom row's own buttons.

props.name: type
props.description: Sets data-type on .ds-popup__body. "text" renders free paragraphs (Penpot's "Summary"); "input" composes a real .ds-input field (Penpot's "Description"); "gallery" composes a real gallery filmstrip plus a gallery-image type="text-icon" selector -- a smaller answer to Penpot's "Image-sliders", see rationale.

props.name: size
props.description: small (500px, Figma's confirmations), medium (800px, Add Description and Summary), or large (1200px, not from a Figma frame yet). Sets data-size on .ds-popup.

props.name: placement
props.description: "center" (default: centered over a full-viewport backdrop dimmed 50%) or "anchored" (marks a confirmation; since 2026-10-13 it is centered exactly like "center", no longer placed under its trigger). Sets data-placement on .ds-popup-overlay.

props.name: backdrop
props.description: static: a click on the backdrop and Escape do not close the popup; only its own [data-popup-dismiss] buttons do. Sets data-backdrop="static" on .ds-popup-overlay. Opt-in per popup, for big forms where a stray click would lose work (the Add project popup); every other popup keeps closing on a backdrop click and Escape.

props.name: preview
props.description: inline: render the popup open, in the page flow (backdrop included), without the hidden attribute -- data-preview="inline". Documentation only (the site's Popups card, Figma D_SYSTEM node 103:4815); never in product UI.

props.name: closable
props.description: Adds a close icon (an X, 24px) at the right edge of the title row. It carries data-popup-dismiss, so it closes the popup like any dismiss button.

rationale:
Styled to Figma's popup-medium (application file, nodes 150:16627, 150:16661, 150:16695, 150:16729), superseding the earlier Penpot values. The panel is bg.surface with no shadow: the dimmed backdrop is what sets it off the page. Title, body and bottom row share one surface with no dividers (as in both design sources), so the panel reads as one plain stack. The title row is 60px with the heading role (heading-4, Inter SemiBold 20). The body has 20px side and 10px vertical padding and scrolls once the panel reaches the viewport; data-type="steps" drops the padding for stacked popup-step sections that carry their own insets. The bottom row is 60px with the actions right-aligned 10px apart; text-button's brackets hang inside each button's 11px padding, so a button is exactly its label plus padding. There is no close (X) control: the design has none, and the bottom row's buttons (plus Escape and a backdrop click) dismiss. Figma's caption slot beside the title and its hidden header action are opacity 0 in every frame and are not modeled.

Sizes: medium 800px (Penpot's panel width; a modal's width is a design decision, not container-driven), small 500px (Figma's confirmation width), large 1173px (Figma's Add project frame, nodes 150:16503 / 150:16475). Backdrop (measured off the design's screens): base/600 gray at 50% behind a centered popup and 30% behind an anchored confirmation. It is a translucent ::before layer, not opacity on the overlay, which would also fade the panel. placement="anchored" sits 10px under its trigger (spacing-3 + spacing-1), never closer than 20px (spacing-6) to a viewport edge, flips above the trigger when it would overflow, and caps its height to the viewport -- measured against documentElement.clientWidth/Height, so a scrollbar gutter doesn't push it past the visible edge.

Body types: "text" (free paragraphs), "input" (Figma's filled textarea, 300px tall in a 320px row), and "gallery" -- a composed gallery filmstrip plus a gallery-image text-icon selector, with a "Reset selection" text-button wired through gallery's generic data-gallery-reset contract, so popup has no gallery-specific code. "gallery" is a deliberately smaller answer to Penpot's "Image-sliders" instance, which nests several sub-widgets that aren't built components.

Behavior (component.js; not sourced -- a design tool doesn't model opening a dialog): a [data-popup-open] trigger shows the matching overlay; any bottom-row button with [data-popup-dismiss] closes it, as do Escape and a backdrop click; both are delegated listeners, so buttons added later work too. Focus moves to the panel on open and back to the trigger on close. Overlays stack: a popup opened from inside another gets a z-index 10 higher (base 100, above dropdown-menu), and Escape and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter act only on the topmost. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter presses the bottom-row action marked data-popup-confirm (template: confirm: true), else a priority=primary one -- every Figma action is a regular-weight secondary button, so primary can't be the only signal. A destructive action (e.g. "Archive selected") uses text-button's error status. Triggers and dismiss buttons are dotted: opening or closing a modal stays in the view. The anchored rule is scoped :not([hidden]) so it never overrides the hidden state. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Close request (2026-10-13): a user-started dismissal (a dismiss button, the backdrop, Escape) first dispatches a cancelable ds-popup-before-close on the overlay (detail: source, button); preventDefault() keeps the popup open, so a host can ask for confirmation first. Scroll lock (explicit request 2026-10-11): while any overlay is open, <html> carries data-popup-scroll-lock and does not scroll, so the wheel moves only the popup body; the native scrollbar width is put back as padding to avoid a sideways shift, and overscroll-behavior: contain stops chaining. It is set from the same stack that stacks overlays, so it clears only when the last one closes. Update 2026-10-14 (explicit request, For You Summary popup): a text body may hold headings, .ds-popup__heading (an h3) in the heading-5 role, 18px, with a blank line above and none between it and its paragraph.
a11y_notes: role="dialog" with aria-labelledby pointing at its title (not in the design source). Implemented: showing and hiding, Escape and backdrop click to close, focus onto the dialog on open and back to the opener on close (also when popups are nested), and Escape / Ctrl+Enter acting only on the topmost popup. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter clicks the confirm button directly, so it is exactly as accessible as clicking it. Tab / Shift+Tab are trapped in the topmost open popup (2026-10-03): Tab from the last focusable control wraps to the first, Shift+Tab from the first or from the panel wraps to the last, and focus outside the popup is pulled back in. The panel keeps a keyboard-only focus ring although Figma draws none. type="gallery" inherits gallery's and gallery-image's own semantics (see their notes). The optional close icon is a real <button aria-label="Close"> outside the title element, so the dialog name stays the title.

name: popup-step
description: One numbered step of a long popup body: a 56px head (numbered title at half opacity, optional text button) over a body that holds the step's control.

props.name: number
props.description: The step's number (the <ol start> value).

props.name: title
props.description: Step title.

props.name: action
props.description: Label of the head's text button (e.g. Reset the selection); omitted when absent.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Makes the step an accordion section: clicking the head (or Enter / Space on the title) shows or hides the body.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: With collapsible: the step starts closed.

props.name: note
props.description: A .ds-popup-step__note in the head, right after the title: a short remark in text-inactive ("No images in this section"); hidden while it has nothing to say.

rationale: The head is 56px (spacing.9 + spacing.5) with 20px side padding, no border and no fill: the popup surface shows through, and steps are separated by their own heads, not by rules. The title is an ordered list with start=N and one item, so the number is real list numbering; the 24px inline-start margin (spacing.7) makes room for it, and the title uses the "title" role at half opacity, like a pane title. The body is inset spacing.cell (10px) / spacing.6 (20px). A .ds-dropdown directly inside a step fills the width. The head's text button hugs its label (see text-button). Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsible (2026-10-12): the head toggles the body that follows it (data-collapsed on the head, so markup stays two siblings); the body animates height over 150ms and is hidden from focus and assistive tech when closed; the open step's title goes to full opacity. window.dsPopupStep.setOpen() lets a host open or close steps from code. Update 2026-10-24 (explicit request): the accordion arrow takes the title's text colour instead of accent-1, so it reads as part of the title; a head may carry a note right after the title in text-inactive body text, for a step that has nothing to choose. A closed step's arrow takes its title's half opacity (grey), an open step's is full (black); the head's text button shows only while the step is open, since it acts on the body (explicit request 2026-10-24).
a11y_notes: Each title is an <ol> with a single <li> so screen readers announce the step number. The head button is a real text-button. Collapsible steps: the title's <li> becomes role=button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, reachable by Tab, toggled by Enter / Space; a closed body is visibility:hidden.

name: progress-bar
description: A thin line that shows how far a running task (e.g. local text recognition) has got, or that it is still running when its progress is unknown.

props.name: value
props.description: 0-100. none (or omitted) renders the indeterminate bar.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name (aria-label).

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node: a spacing-1 (4px) line in accent-1 under the flow's header. The track is border-table, the hairline color, so the empty part reads as part of the layout, not as a second control. The width comes from data-value via component.js into a private --_progress, so a host passes data, never a style value. Indeterminate (no value) moves a third-width fill across the track: the animation is functional, it is the only sign that a long local task is still running, and it stops under prefers-reduced-motion (the fill then shows full width at reduced opacity). Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: role=progressbar with aria-valuemin/max and aria-valuenow (omitted while indeterminate), and an aria-label.

name: radio
description: A radio option drawn as a text button with a round Figma marker (ring in the accent color, filled when checked). Compose several in a .ds-radio-group.

props.name: options
props.description: Each option: { value, label, checked }.

props.name: label
props.description: aria-label of the radiogroup.

rationale: An option is a real .ds-text-button with role=radio, so it keeps the text button's type, underline and focus ring. The marker is CSS only: a ring spacing.8 / 2 (16px) in the accent color drawn with an inset shadow, and a spacing.9 / 4 (10px) dot when aria-checked is true, centered in a 24px (spacing.7) box. The text button's hover "[ ]" is removed (content: none) because the marker already shows which option is under the pointer. Height is spacing.9 (40px); options stack with a spacing.cell (10px) gap. Not sourced from Figma: the roving tabindex and arrow-key behavior in component.js. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: role="radiogroup" with role="radio" options and aria-checked. Only the checked option is in the tab order (roving tabindex); arrow keys move and check.

name: sidebar-item
description: One entry in a sidebar list (sidebar-list composes several). type="set": one row of a sets sidebar (a clickable name, optional save toggle). type="card": a subtitle, a saved-icon, a title and a status line. type="button": a single primary action. Renamed from Penpot's "Sidebar" to avoid colliding with the composed list, which this system names sidebar-list.

props.name: type
props.description: "card" renders the subtitle/title/status card (Penpot's Default/PDF Downloaded/Submitted States -- identical layout, only the status text differs, so not modeled as three separate types); "button" renders a single centered .ds-text-button instead (Penpot's own "Button" State) -- not a card at all. "set" (not from Penpot, see rationale) renders a clickable set-name button + toggleable save icon on one row, one caption line below.

props.name: name
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". The set's name, rendered as a clickable secondary text-button (selects the set), truncated with an ellipsis when it overflows.

props.name: caption
props.description: type="set": optional second line under the name, in grey (text-active at half opacity, the same grey as table-cell's text-passive-cell) -- e.g. a record's status. The row grows to two lines; without it the set row stays the single 44px line. (Kept from the earlier Penpot set card; shown again since 2026-09-30.)

props.name: saved
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". Initial data-saved state for the save icon; component.js keeps it in sync on click and dispatches ds-sidebar-item-favourite-toggle.

props.name: active
props.description: type="set": marks the active set (fill and hairlines above and below).

props.name: muted
props.description: type="set": a record that needs no more action (e.g. an application already sent). Its name is grey at rest and takes the accent back on hover, focus, or when active.

props.name: href
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". When given, the set name renders as an <a href> (still the same secondary/dotted text-button) instead of a <button data-select-set> -- for a sidebar whose rows navigate, e.g. an in-page section index (dotted, because it stays on the page; CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Passed through the safe_url filter.

props.name: save
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". false omits the save button entirely (a navigation row has nothing to save). Default true.

rationale:
type="set" (Figma sets sidebar): a 44px row with the set's name as a text button and a 44px save button with Figma's bookmark icons (aria-pressed toggles them); the active set (data-active) is filled and ruled above and below, and its name uses the body-text medium weight, so the current set stands out without a new type scale. The saved icon is accent-1, the same as table-cell's row-level favourite: one save flag, one color, wherever it renders. With `href`, the name renders as an <a> (navigation, e.g. an in-page section index) instead of a <button>, and save=false omits the save button; one row layout serves both uses. Rows deviate from text-button's hover brackets: on hover and focus the whole row takes bg.surface-pressed, as table-row does, and the name gets no brackets -- the full-width fill already marks the click target. The dotted underline stays. A long name truncates with an ellipsis (the composed text button can shrink: flex 1 1 auto, min-width 0).

type="card" and type="button" (Penpot "Sidebar" states Default, PDF Downloaded, Submitted, Button): the main section is a space-between row and the sub section a column with rowGap spacing-3, both Token-bound in Penpot. Card padding is spacing-2 / spacing-5. Colors are read off the text layers: subtitle accent-1 (the one colored identifier a reader scans the list for), title text-active, status text-subactive. The saved icon is object-dark-active at spacing-7 (24px), like every other icon-only glyph. Width is 100%, because a sidebar's width comes from its container, not from Penpot's 340px demo board. type="button" is shorter (70px vs 84px) and centered, holding one primary text-button, as Penpot's own instance is. Selecting, linking or adding records is the host application's concern. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Set rows follow Figma D_SYSTEM 28:1718 (default), 28:1721 (hover: base/100 fill with base/300 hairlines) and 188:4543 (selected: base/150 fill in light, black Medium name without underline, hairlines). Added 2026-10-12. Save visibility (2026-10-19, explicit request): on an inactive, unsaved set the save button is opacity 0 until the row is hovered or focused; the active set, a saved set (its mark is information) and the create row keep theirs at all times.
a11y_notes: type="set": the name is a real <button> (or <a> with href; the active row gets aria-current), and the save control is a real <button> with aria-pressed and an aria-label naming the set, so both are keyboard-operable. type="card": the saved-icon is a decorative role="img" span with an aria-label, not a control -- the design shows no affordance on it. type="button" is a real <button> via text-button.

name: sidebar-list
description: A sets sidebar: a 280px column with a 60px head (title, collapse toggle) over a scrolling list of sidebar-item type="set" rows, optionally opened by a 56px create row. Collapses to a 64px strip.

props.name: title
props.description: Head title, shown at half opacity.

props.name: create
props.description: Label of the create row, the first item of the list (a primary text-button in a type="set" sidebar-item with data-role="create"). Omit for none. Its height is the pane heads' (56px), so it lines up with them.

props.name: label
props.description: aria-label of the sidebar.

props.name: items
props.description: Set rows: { name, saved, active, href?, save? } -- href/save pass through to sidebar-item type="set" (see its meta.json): href makes the row a link, save=false drops its save button.

rationale: Width is spacing.9 x 7 (280px), collapsed spacing.row + 2 x spacing.cell (64px). The head is 60px (spacing.9 + spacing.6, changed from 56px on 2026-10-11 so it lines up with the page head beside it) with 10px padding and one hairline below; the optional create row is 56px (spacing.9 + spacing.5, the pane head's height) and every other row keeps the sidebar-item height; the title is the "title" role (Inter SemiBold 16px) at half opacity; the toggle is a 44 x 40px bordered button holding the accent-colored arrow (a CSS mask, so it takes the accent color), flipped when collapsed. The list has no rules between rows: only the active set is ruled, inside sidebar-item, so the one row that matters stands out. Surface is bg.surface with a right hairline in object-dark.passive in both themes (the design has no separate dark value yet). Collapse behavior and its ARIA state live in component.js; choosing and saving sets is the host page's concern (sidebar-item exposes data-select-set / data-save-set hooks). Replaces an earlier Penpot card sidebar. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsed (updated 2026-10-12): the sidebar stays a 64px strip in the page flow; the toggle slides the full panel open over the page (clip-path 200ms, data-peek) without moving the layout, and a click outside, Escape or choosing a row closes it. The create row follows Figma D_SYSTEM 28:1729: 45px, bold dotted-underlined name, a plus in the icon cell, a closing hairline. A create row can be busy (data-busy, 2026-10-25): its plus becomes the loading glyph, turning while the host's action runs, and the row takes no clicks. Update 2026-10-25 (explicit request): collapsing and pinning open are animated as well, 200ms: the panel edge travels between full width and strip and the page beside it follows; peeking still slides over the page without moving it. Driven by two registered fractions (--_sb-in for the flow, --_sb-shown for the clip), so resizing stays immediate. Same day, "super smooth": the flow now switches at once and component.js slides the elements after the sidebar with a compositor transform (FLIP), since animating the margin laid the whole page out on every frame; only the clip of the panel itself is transitioned.
a11y_notes: An <aside> with aria-label. The toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and a label that flips between Collapse sidebar and Expand sidebar (on a collapsed sidebar the toggle pins it open, also while hover has it slid open); each set row's name and save buttons are real buttons (the save button uses aria-pressed).

name: skeleton
description: A grey placeholder in the shape of what is loading (a table row, a sidebar item, a block, a paper sheet, a picture). Shown while a container waits for its data, removed when the content renders; a picture is its own placeholder until its pixels arrive.

props.name: variant
props.description: "row" (small square plus bars), "item" (one bar, sidebar), "block" (two lines, CV block) or "page" (a landscape sheet, preview panes). A picture does not take this prop: class ds-skeleton-image goes on the itself.

rationale: Pages used to show empty containers (or false empty states) until their API calls returned. A skeleton shows the shape of what is coming: bars at the width of typical cells, in bg.surface-pressed, pulsing in opacity (1.4s, still under prefers-reduced-motion). It is declarative: data-skeleton="row:4" on a container, filled by component.js when the HTML is parsed, cleared as soon as real content is added to the container (or with dsSkeleton.clear()); a 10s fail-safe clears it anyway. grid-column: 1 / -1 makes one placeholder span all columns of a grid table. [data-skeleton-hide] hides an empty state meanwhile. Not sourced from Figma (explicit request 2026-10-12). Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Update 2026-10-20 (explicit request): data-static on a hand-written .ds-skeleton draws the shape without the pulse and component.js leaves it in place when the page data arrives; used for the blank sheets of an empty preview. Update 2026-10-25 (explicit request, "a skeleton for pictures that load"): class ds-skeleton-image on an makes the picture its own placeholder: its box is the same grey, pulsing, until the pixels arrive, then the picture fades in over 450ms (fade-in's timing). component.js marks it data-loaded (loaded; instant when it was already loaded on insertion, so a redrawn view does not flash; error, which keeps a still grey). Made for lazily loaded pictures (loading="lazy"), which arrive at any time: a long preview loads only the pictures in view, and the others show their boxes meanwhile. fade-in leaves these pictures to the skeleton.
a11y_notes: Placeholders are aria-hidden; the container carries aria-busy="true" while they are shown. The pulse is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. A picture placeholder keeps the img's own alt; its pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion too.

name: stepper
description: The steps of a short multi-step flow in one row (e.g. upload a photo, check the recognized text, done), the current step marked and earlier steps checked off.

props.name: steps
props.description: Step labels, in order. Plain text.

props.name: current
props.description: 1-based index of the current step. Steps before it are done (check mark), steps after it are to do.

props.name: label
props.description: aria-label of the list.

props.name: done_label
props.description: Accessible name of a done step's check mark.

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node. Orientation, not content: the data typography role in uppercase and text-subactive, like a table's header labels. The current step is told apart by color (text-active) and by shape (a solid underline of border-width-default, offset spacing-2), so it does not depend on color alone; it is not accent-1 and not dotted, so it does not read as a link (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). The steps are not clickable: the flow moves by its own buttons. A done step's check mark is two borders of a rotated box in currentColor, because the icon set has no check icon (checkbox-selected is a filled box); flagged rather than adding an icon. The canvas used the base-750 primitive for the inactive steps; text-subactive is the themed semantic token for it. aria-current="step" marks the current step for assistive technology. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: An ordered list with an aria-label; the current step has aria-current="step"; the check mark is role=img with an accessible name.

name: table-cell
description: A single cell within a table-row of a queue table: text data, an icon/checkbox slot, a link, a dropdown/input field, or an action-button slot, depending on `type`. table-row composes several of these per row; header-block's divider marks the boundary between the header and the first row of cells.

props.name: type
props.description: Which cell kind this renders: checkbox-cell (was Penpot's "icon"), icon-cell (was "saved" and "action-icons", merged into one type that holds any number of icons), date, text-active-cell (was "title", "organisation" and "description", already identical), text-passive-cell (was "source"), text-subactive-cell (was "summary"), link, 1-action, 2-actions, 3-actions, dropdown, input, empty-state, status-label, tag. See rationale.

props.name: content
props.description: The cell's text content, for text-bearing types (date, text-active-cell, text-passive-cell, text-subactive-cell, link, dropdown, input, tag). Not applicable to checkbox-cell, icon-cell, 1-action, 2-actions, 3-actions, or empty-state, which have fixed or composed content. For 1-action/2-actions/3-actions, doubles as the primary (rightmost) button's label.

props.name: tag_type
props.description: Only for type="tag": the tag's type (accent-1 | accent-2 | accent-3 | success | warning | danger | neutral), passed to the composed tag.

props.name: tag_subtype
props.description: Only for type="tag": active or passive, passed to the composed tag.

props.name: article
props.description: Only for type="link": der | die | das colors the link by grammatical gender (der keeps accent-1, die row-status-declined-text, das row-status-approved-text). Other values are ignored.

props.name: checkbox_role
props.description: Only meaningful when type="checkbox-cell". Unset (default): the normal row-select checkbox (unchecked / checked), toggled by table-row off the row's data-selected. "select-all": adds a third icon (checkbox-semi-select) and marks the cell data-checkbox-role="select-all", so table-row's select-all logic and table-cell's [data-state] rules can target it. Not sourced from the design.

props.name: editable
props.description: Text-bearing types only (not checkbox-cell/icon-cell/dropdown/input/1-action/2-actions/3-actions/empty-state/status-label). Renders a hidden .ds-input sibling alongside the text span and marks the cell data-editable so a same-row [data-edit-trigger] button (see extra_attrs) can toggle it into edit mode -- see component.js.

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="1-action" (and as the primary button's attrs for "2-actions"/"3-actions"). Raw attribute string passed through to the composed text-button's own extra_attrs passthrough (see text-button/template.html) -- e.g. extra_attrs='data-edit-trigger' to wire an Edit button at a row's own editable cell, the same pattern popup already uses for data-popup-open/dismiss.

props.name: secondary_extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="2-actions"/"3-actions". Same passthrough as extra_attrs, but for the secondary (middle, Dismiss-style) button instead of the primary one.

props.name: tertiary_label
props.description: Only meaningful for type="3-actions". Label for the leftmost, lowest-emphasis of the 3 buttons (secondary priority, same as the middle button).

props.name: tertiary_extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="3-actions". Same passthrough as extra_attrs/secondary_extra_attrs, but for the tertiary (leftmost) button.

props.name: options
props.description: Only meaningful when type="dropdown". A list of { value, label }: when given, the input-dropdown trigger is wired (data-dropdown-trigger) inside a .ds-dropdown wrapper with a dropdown-menu of these items, so the cell's dropdown actually opens (link components/dropdown-menu's component.js on the page). Omitted: the unwired trigger alone, unchanged.

props.name: dropdown_label
props.description: Only meaningful with options. The trigger's aria-label (the visible text is the current value, not what the control is for).

props.name: view_label
props.description: Text-bearing types only. Renders Figma's "Single-active-t+button" cell (D_SYSTEM node 28:949): the text clipped to one line with an ellipsis, followed by a secondary dotted text-button with this label (e.g. "view") that stays whole. The host page wires the button (e.g. to a popup showing the full text).

props.name: submit
props.description: Only for type "1-action": the action button is a submit button of the enclosing form.

props.name: plain
props.description: Only for type="link": no underline; without an article the link takes the text color and turns accent-1 while its row is hovered or focused. For a row whose whole area is the link (table-row href).

props.name: mark
props.description: Text-bearing types: a short count after the text (e.g. '✗1'), in the declined status colors -- how often this form was wrong.

props.name: mark_label
props.description: Accessible name of the mark (e.g. 'wrong once').

props.name: highlight
props.description: 'success' fills the cell with row-status-approved-bg and its text with row-status-approved-text (the answer in a rule table).

props.name: wrap
props.description: Text-bearing types: show the whole text wrapped over as many lines as it needs instead of one clipped line; the cell and its row siblings drop the fixed row height (the row-height floor stays as a min-height). Sets data-wrap.

rationale:
Layout (Figma flat table): every cell is one table row high -- spacing.row (44px) plus a 1px object-dark-passive hairline under it -- with spacing.cell (10px) padding, on bg.surface, and no vertical rules. Text is one line with an ellipsis; .ds-table-cell__clip clips an excerpt beside an inline "view" button. Cells share the row's width (flex 1 1 0%); fixed-content types (checkbox-cell, icon-cell, input, the action types, status-label) are flex: none and size to their content. Link cells right-align and never wrap (at most two lines, accent-1, underline on hover). Action cells left-align with a 16px right padding. A dropdown or input cell lets its field fill the cell; the input keeps its box border in the cell (Figma's table rows draw it), although input's transparent fill is borderless elsewhere.

Types: started as Penpot's 15 Type values and were merged where Penpot's own cells were identical. text-active-cell (was title / organisation / description -- pixel-identical in Penpot) is text.active body text; text-passive-cell (was source) and text-subactive-cell (was summary; body-text italic) keep Penpot's identifiers; icon-cell (was saved and action-icons) holds any number of icons, adopting action-icons' multi-icon layout, a deliberate deviation for a lone saved icon; checkbox-cell (was icon) is Penpot's generic single-icon cell, also used for the drag handle. Penpot's State axis is "Value 1" (an unused placeholder) on almost every type, so there is no `state` prop: hover lives in the composed controls. Composition, not restyling: action cells compose text-button, dropdown and input cells compose input-dropdown and input.

Icons: every glyph is the Figma D_SYSTEM set (node 103:4711) in icons/, inlined by component.js so currentColor and --_icon-fill / --_icon-mark apply. Checkbox and save rest as an input-icon outline on an input-fill box (input-icon rather than Figma's text-inactive, which disappears on the dark surface) and turn accent on hover; a selected checkbox is an accent box with an inverse mark; a saved bookmark fills with accent-2. checkbox-cell carries both an unchecked and a checked icon, and table-row's CSS swaps them off the row's data-selected, so selection needs no extra script. The checkbox styling is scoped to [data-icon="checkbox"], so a drag glyph in the same cell layout isn't recolored; data-icon="drag" paints Figma's drag glyph.

Row actions: in light, active action buttons rest in text-inactive (like an inactive tab title) and turn accent-1 while their row is hovered, focused or selected (Figma node 237:31166), so a long table isn't a wall of blue; disabled, loading, error and unread buttons keep their own color. Dark keeps them accent, because dark's text-inactive would not read on its background. 1-action, 2-actions and 3-actions share one shape (row, left-aligned, flex: none); 3-actions has no Penpot instance and follows 2-actions.

Additions not sourced from the design: `editable` renders the text and a hidden .ds-input side by side and toggles hidden, so the cell's size never changes between states; the trigger is a row's own button (extra_attrs='data-edit-trigger'), because editing sits behind an explicit action. extra_attrs / secondary_extra_attrs / tertiary_extra_attrs pass raw attributes through to the composed text-buttons (author markup, never user data). status-label is a plain, non-interactive span in system-success replacing an action group once a record is done -- not a disabled button, since there is nothing to click. `checkbox_role="select-all"` adds a third, semi-selected icon for a header checkbox that table-row drives. Shift+click on a Save icon saves or unsaves the range since the last Save click in the same table (visible rows, DOM order), dispatched as one ds-table-cell-favourite-toggle event with detail.range = true. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsed excerpt (explicit request 2026-10-11, threshold changed 2026-10-12): a text cell is an ellipsized excerpt (.ds-table-cell__clip) followed by a text button, usually "view". A button carrying data-collapse-label opts in: the excerpt is shown only when the column leaves room for as much text as "Dear Artist, This October, ARRIVAL Gallery will bring artists" in the excerpt's own font (the room is the cell's text box minus the button, the same in every row, so a column collapses entirely or not at all; re-measured on every width change and for cells added later). With less room component.js sets data-collapsed on the .ds-table-cell__text, style.css hides the excerpt, and the button is renamed after the field ("Summary", "Full Description") and lines up like a button standing in for column text. Other cells are untouched. The sample text is a constant in component.js because it is a behavior, not a style value.

The notes field's "Add a note" placeholder is hidden (opacity 0) until its row is hovered or something in the row has focus: empty fields on every row would repeat the same hint down the column. Typed text is unaffected. Additions 2026-10-23 (application design canvas, no Figma node): plain links (data-plain) drop the underline because the whole row is the target, so an underline on one cell would mislabel the click area; a non-gendered plain link uses the text color at rest and accent-1 while its row is hovered (the row's hover is the affordance), in both themes. mark is a data-role count on row-status-declined-bg / -text, so a form table shows where the mistakes are in place, with an accessible name. highlight='success' is the approved row-status pair (themed; the signal-success primitives stay light in the dark theme), for the one cell that is the answer.
a11y_notes: type="dropdown" renders a real .ds-input-dropdown <button> (listen for its ds-input-dropdown-open event); type="input" a real <input type="text">; type="link" a real <a href>. Icon cells use role="img" with an aria-label per icon, since each icon is its own unit; the inlined SVGs carry no separate text. Icons are fetched at runtime relative to the script's own URL (so they work wherever the system is vendored), and need http(s): from file:// the icon slots stay empty. Known gaps: the Save icon toggles on click but stays role="img" with no aria-pressed and no keyboard handler, so its state isn't announced and it is pointer-only, as is Shift+click range saving; `editable`'s switch to the input moves focus but isn't announced, and the input has no label. status-label is plain text. type="tag" is plain inline text (see tag): the label carries the meaning, color only reinforces it.

name: table-footer
description: The row under a table's last row that loads more of it ("Load 10 more", "Load all 100"): a 44px row on the pressed surface whose first button aligns with the third column's text.

props.name: first_label
props.description: Label of the first (text-aligned) button.

props.name: second_label
props.description: Label of the second button.

props.name: first_action
props.description: data-action value of the first button, for the host page to listen for.

props.name: second_action
props.description: data-action value of the second button.

rationale: Height is one table row: spacing.row (44px) plus the 1px hairline, like every table row. Fill is bg.surface-pressed (Figma base/100). The hairline is border.muted (base/150), with object-dark.passive as the fallback because border.muted has no dark value yet. Left padding is two 44px icon columns plus the 10px cell padding, so the first button's label starts where the Name column's text starts: the first button is a text-aligned button (no left padding, hover "[" hung outside the label), exactly like table-cell's text-active-cell button. Not sourced from Figma: the data-action hooks, through which the host page attaches its own load behavior; no behavior lives in the component. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Two real <button> elements; keyboard focus uses text-button's own focus ring. The row has no landmark role: it is part of the table's section.

name: table-header
description: The title region of a table's header-block: either a single section title, a two-tab selector (e.g. switching between status views), or a title paired with a secondary info caption (e.g. page count). Sits to the left of table-header-actions inside header-block. Standalone, it renders as its own shaded/bordered chip (see rationale); nested inside header-block, that chip is reset to plain, since header-block's own row now carries the same shading across its full width instead (see components/header-block/meta.json).

props.name: type
props.description: 1-tab (single title), 2-tabs (two clickable labels, one active/one inactive), or title-info (title + subactive caption). Maps to Penpot's `type` variant axis; Penpot's own values were kebab-cased ("1 Tab" -> "1-tab", etc.).

rationale:
All three variants share two Token-bound values from Penpot's instances: a left inset of spacing.6 (20px) and, when there is a second element, a column gap of spacing.5 (16px). Title and tab labels use the heading-4 role; the component never uses bold heading weights. type="2-tabs" encodes selection with color alone: the selected tab is text.active, the other text.inactive -- the system's existing active/inactive vocabulary. Clicking is wired in component.js because an active/inactive pair with no way to switch would be a dead affordance; the static design source doesn't model the click. type="title-info" pairs the title with a bodyText caption in text.subactive, the token for de-emphasized but legible secondary text (e.g. "3 pages"). An optional `info` caption on 2-tabs (not sourced from Penpot) reuses the same caption styling, for a count under the tabs; without `info`, 2-tabs renders unchanged.

Standalone, the component is a shaded chip: bg.surface-pressed with the border-width-thin / object-dark-passive border table-cell's grid uses, so it reads as part of the same bordered table. This is a deliberate deviation from Penpot, whose instances carry no background or border, modeled on a wikitable caption. bg.surface-pressed was chosen because it moves in the theme-appropriate emphasis direction in both palettes. Sizing stays content-hugging, because the component is a flex child of header-block's row next to table-header-actions. Inside header-block, the row itself carries the shading across its full width, so header-block/style.css resets this chip's background, border and padding there to avoid a doubled box. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: type="2 Tabs" renders as role="tablist" with role="tab"/aria-selected on each label per WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, since Penpot's design implies exactly that interaction (one selected, one not, click to switch). type="1-tab" and "title-info" render as plain text (no tab semantics, since there's nothing to select between). The new optional caption on "2-tabs" is a plain <span>, outside the tablist's own role semantics (a caption describing table contents, not a third tab).

name: table-header-actions
description: The action-button cluster docked at the right side of a table's header-block (e.g. "Add item", "Export", "Clear filters"). A row of 1-4 text-button instances, ordered from least to most emphasis with the single primary action always last/rightmost. Renamed from Penpot's literal component name "table-header_right-block" (see rationale).
rationale: Renamed from Penpot's "table-header_right-block": the schema's name pattern rejects the underscore. Penpot's Actions axis values ("1 Action" ... "3 Actions", and inconsistently "4") are normalized to "1-action" ... "4-actions". The component is only a flex-row shell: column gap 0 (Token-confirmed in Penpot -- the buttons' own padding separates them) and right padding 0, because header-block's row already carries the 20px side padding and the buttons hug their labels. It composes real text-button instances rather than restyling buttons, because Penpot's source is itself composition: every child in every sampled instance is a text-button (no fill token, only a label). The emphasis pattern read off the instances: each extra action is lower emphasis, and the single primary action is always last, rightmost. Every sampled action (Add item, Export, Clear filters, Select all) acts within the current table view, so all use the dotted underline (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Each action may carry a `status` (text-button's, default 'active'), so bulk actions can render disabled until rows are selected, `submit` (true: a form submit button) and `extra_attrs` (raw attribute passthrough, e.g. form="id"). It sets no background, so header-block's shaded row shows through behind its buttons. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.

name: table-header-cell
description: A single column-header cell for a table's header row: a plain label, a sort button with a direction arrow when the column is sortable, and/or a favourite-all toggle for a Save column. Sibling cells sharing one [data-sort-group] container sort exclusively -- only one column at a time.

props.name: sortable
props.description: When true, renders the label inside a clickable sort button with a direction-arrow icon. When false, renders a plain, non-interactive label (unless favourite_all is also set).

props.name: label
props.description: The column's header text.

props.name: sort_dir
props.description: Initial data-sort-dir: none, asc, or desc. Only meaningful when sortable=true.

props.name: favourite_all
props.description: For a Save column's header cell: adds a favourite-all toggle beside the sort button -- two independent click targets, the icon toggles every row's saved state and the arrow sorts by it. Sets data-favourite-all / data-type="icon-cell" on the cell so table-row's updateFavouriteAllState() and table-cell's favourite listener drive it (see rationale).

props.name: all_saved
props.description: Initial data-saved state for the favourite-all button. Only meaningful when favourite_all=true; table-row/component.js's updateFavouriteAllState() keeps it in sync at runtime once rows exist.

props.name: filter
props.description: Renders the label as a button that opens a dropdown-menu of values, for a column whose rows can be narrowed to one value. Sets data-filter / data-filter-value on the cell. Takes precedence over sortable. The page needs dropdown-menu's style.css and component.js as well.

props.name: filter_options
props.description: The values after the first item, each { value, label }. Only meaningful when filter=true. With filter_multiple, an option with selected=false starts unticked (every other one starts ticked).

props.name: filter_all_label
props.description: Label of the first item, whose value is "" and which clears the filter. Only meaningful when filter=true.

props.name: filter_icon
props.description: Only meaningful when filter=true. The icons/<name>.svg glyph beside the label: "arrow" (default) or "filter" -- Figma D_SYSTEM's filter glyph (node 38:2934), which its All table uses on a filterable column header.

props.name: filter_multiple
props.description: Only meaningful when filter=true. The menu is dropdown-menu's checkbox list (multiple=true), so several values show at once; the first item (filter_all_label) ticks or clears all. Sets data-filter-multiple and data-filter-values (the ticked values, space-separated) on the cell; ds-table-header-cell-filter carries { values }.

rationale:
Not built from a design-source instance: neither Penpot nor Figma had a column header with a sort affordance when it was built. It generalizes a working pattern from this repo's earlier sample table (site.css / site.js); every visual value was already token-bound there. Styled since to Figma's header cell (Table cell, header-cell text+icon: default 35:8275, hovered 35:8396, selected 35:8423) and the flat table: 44px plus a 1px hairline like a row. Labels use the "data" role (Inter Medium 13px, uppercase) in both themes -- type doesn't depend on the theme -- in the header-cell-label token (base/600) in light and text-subactive in dark.

Sortable: default is the header gray on the plain cell; hovered is black on base/100; selected -- the column with data-sort-dir asc or desc -- is the accent color on base/100, label and arrow always sharing one color. The label keeps its dotted underline (sorting stays in the view) and the 24px arrow (icons/arrow-down.svg) stays visible in every state, 10px from the label. The sort and favourite-all buttons carry the 10px cell padding, so the whole cell is clickable. Siblings in one [data-sort-group] sort exclusively. The component doesn't reorder rows: it cycles data-sort-dir and dispatches a bubbling event, and the host sorts its own rows -- a reusable header can't know the host table's row shape.

favourite_all: a Save column's header needs two independent click targets in one cell -- the icon toggles every row's saved state, a separate arrow sorts by it. The cell carries data-favourite-all and data-type="icon-cell" so table-row's updateFavouriteAllState() and table-cell's favourite listener drive it; the icon markup is hand-matched to table-cell's icon-cell (a nested .ds-table-cell would draw a doubled box), so it isn't declared in `uses`, and the icon-cell padding it picks up is reset for the header layout.

Filter (no design-source node): a header cell whose label opens a dropdown-menu of values. It reuses the sortable header's three states (selected = a value is chosen or the menu is open) and the 24px arrow, or Figma D_SYSTEM's filter glyph (node 38:2934) with filter_icon="filter". The label keeps the column's name. The component records the choice (data-filter-value, accent state, aria-selected) and dispatches ds-table-header-cell-filter with {value, label}; the host narrows its rows. The dropdown wrapper and menu markup are hand-matched, so dropdown-menu isn't in `uses` and a host links its CSS and JS itself. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Filter, multiple (explicit request 2026-10-01: a Status column that shows several statuses at once, all but Archived and Filtered by default): the same header button, with dropdown-menu's checkbox list (included, so the item markup has one source). Its "All" item is ticked when every value is and half-ticked when only some are; the button is accent while any value is left out, the same "this column is filtered" state as the single filter. Column resize (explicit request 2026-10-01, no design source): opt-in with data-column-resize on the grid container (its value a name; the widths are not remembered across a reload, explicit request 2026-10-12, and a value stored by an earlier version under "ds-columns:<name>" is cleared). Each header cell but the last column gets pane's split handle on its right edge (8px grab area inside the cell, 2px accent line on hover, focus and drag). Dragging moves a column's right border and the columns after it share the difference in proportion (none under the minimum), so the table keeps its width and the columns to the left stay put; arrow keys move it 24px, a double click restores the CSS widths. Sizes are applied as data-columns-resized + --_column-sizes (minmax(0, <px>fr) per column, so a resized table keeps its proportions at another window width), never under spacing.9, and a column marked data-resize-min="content" (on its header cell or a wrapper around it) never under what its content needs: measured at the start of each drag by laying the grid out once with those columns at max-content, and kept as the track's CSS floor (minmax(max-content, ...)) so content that grows later still fits (explicit request 2026-10-01: buttons, a checkbox or a status never squeezed until they no longer fit); cells in a resized table drop their min-width so a column can be narrower than its content. Each drag, arrow step or reset fires ds-table-columns-resize { before, after } (px, or null for the CSS widths) and the container takes ds-table-columns-set { sizes } back, so a host can undo a resize (the consuming app's Ctrl+Z).
a11y_notes: The sort button is a native <button> with an aria-label ("Sort by <label>") stating the action; the direction is in data-sort-dir and not announced separately -- a host using a real <table> could add aria-sort on the header cell (the component assumes a CSS grid of divs, like table-row). Filter: the trigger is a native <button> with aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-expanded kept by dropdown-menu, and an aria-label naming the column and, once chosen, the value ("Filter by Type: Analysed"); the menu is a role="listbox" of role="option" buttons with aria-selected on the chosen one. Escape and an outside click close it. Filter, multiple: the menu is aria-multiselectable; aria-label lists the shown values while some are left out ("Filter by Status: For review, Analysed"). Column resize: each handle is a focusable role="separator" (aria-orientation vertical, aria-label "Resize <label>"); ArrowLeft / ArrowRight move the border 24px.

name: table-preview
description: Every table type of the Figma D_SYSTEM table-row frame in one table: All, For review, Analyzed, Archived, Filtered, Queue, Collection, Reference and Draft, each with its own column set, one shown at a time. The Type column's header is a filter that switches the type; All shows every ticket with the All table's columns. Sortable Category / Due date / Status headers, a Status filter on All, and per-row Status dropdowns that recolor the row's status pill.

props.name: types
props.description: [{ id, label, columns, actions, in_all }]. columns: the column keys in order (template.html's COLUMNS: drag (a Reorder handle: drag the row up/down, via table-row), check, save, name, category, due, summary, type, status, status_sort, reason, details, dates, link, notes, updates, actions). actions: the table-cell spec of that type's Actions cell. in_all: whether that type's records appear in the first type's table. The first type is the combined one (All); its label is the Type filter's first item.

props.name: records
props.description: [{ type, status, name, category, due, summary, reason, details, dates, notes, updates }] -- one row each, in its own type's table (and in the first table if its type has in_all). A field a column does not use is ignored; a column whose field is missing renders empty.

props.name: status_options
props.description: [{ value, label }] offered by every Status dropdown and by All's Status filter. value is what the row's data-status becomes (table-row colors the pill for analysed / submitted / approved / pending / declined).

props.name: active
props.description: The type id shown at load. Default: the first type.

rationale: Figma draws each table type as a separate Header + Table pair stacked down the table-row frame; this component puts them in one table so the column sets can be compared by switching. Column sets, header kinds and cell kinds are Figma's (see source): Category and Due date headers carry the sort arrow, All's Status header the filter glyph (icons/filter.svg, node 38:2934), Queue's Status the arrow; Summary / Reason cells are Figma's Single-active-t+button cell (text clipped, "view" kept whole); Status cells are dropdowns whose value is a pill in the row-status colors. One deliberate deviation: Figma's Full Description column is replaced by Type, whose header is the filter that picks the type, so the switch lives in the table's own vocabulary (a filterable column) rather than a separate control; types without Full Description (Collection, Template, Queue) get Type right after Name. Every cell is a real include of table-cell, table-header-cell or table-row; this component adds only the grid (one per type, so header and body share tracks via display:contents rows), the hidden-row fix display:contents needs, and the host wiring the composed components leave to their page (filter, sort, status). All nine types are rendered at build time and hidden, not built by script, because the composed components wire their behavior once at load. Column tracks are token-based: flexible text columns are minmax(spacing-9 x 4, 1fr), everything else max-content (Figma's fixed widths are the width of their content). Actions sit at 40% until row hover (data-reveal-actions), as Figma draws them. An optional `drag` column (blank header, table-row's drag handle) lets a table offer row reordering. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Each type's grid is role="table" labelled with the type's name; hidden tables are removed from the accessibility tree by the hidden attribute. The Type and Status filters are table-header-cell filter buttons (aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-label naming the column and the current choice); the row Status dropdowns carry aria-label "Status of <name>". Rows are grid items via display:contents, so there is no row role; screen readers read the cells in order. Selection, save and dropdown keyboard behavior are the composed components' own.

name: table-row
description: One row of a queue table: a horizontal composition of table-cell instances (checkbox-cell, text cells, status, date, icon-cell, row actions), with a selected state toggled by clicking the row's own checkbox. table-row defines no cell content itself -- it is a flex container that composes table-cell. The demo shows every row Type of the Penpot source with its real cell composition and order, plus a block of rows stacked together with a header row.

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the row is selected (Penpot's State axis, Default / Selected): its cells fill bg.surface-pressed and its checkbox shows the checked icon, both by CSS off this attribute. Toggled only by clicking the row's own checkbox (component.js).

props.name: status
props.description: Optional data-status on the row (analysed / submitted / approved / pending / declined): style.css colors the value of the row's dropdown-type cell as a status pill from the row-status tokens. Other values, or none, leave it plain.

props.name: flash
props.description: Optional data-flash="success" on the row: its cells fade from system-success back to their own fill once, over three seconds (a result just landed). The host sets it and removes it on animationend; no animation under prefers-reduced-motion. The green starts weaker in the dark theme.

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Raw attribute passthrough on the row element (e.g. a data-* identifier the host page reads back). Same contract as text-button's extra_attrs: the host passes only trusted, pre-escaped markup.

props.name: href
props.description: data-href on the row: a click anywhere in the row that is not on a control opens this URL (component.js). Keep a link cell in the row for keyboard and middle-click. Before navigating, a cancelable ds-table-row-open { href } event is dispatched on the row; preventDefault() keeps the page (a host opening the row in place).

props.name: cells
props.description: Cell dicts passed to table-cell. Keys passed through: type, content, icons, secondary_label, input_value, href, single_icon, single_icon_label, priority, checkbox_role, options, dropdown_label, view_label, tag_type, tag_subtype, article, plain, mark, mark_label, highlight, wrap, submit, extra_attrs, secondary_extra_attrs, tertiary_label, tertiary_extra_attrs.

props.name: action-row
props.description: data-action-row on a row-like element (display:contents, not a .ds-table-row) whose whole width is one action: row hover fill and the pointer; the host makes a click on it press its button.

props.name: visited
props.description: data-visited="true": the viewer has already acted on this row; its cells take bg-row-visited.

rationale:
Only Penpot's State axis (Default | Selected) is a style variant. Its other axes -- Type (Checkbox only, Analysed, Found, Archived, Submitted, Empty State, Collection, Check + Button, Snippet) and Comment -- only change which table-cells are composed, never the row's own CSS, so they are demo compositions, not props (as header-block treats its Type axis). Each Type's composition was read off its Penpot instance by x-position, not DOM order: Penpot authors rows in row-reverse with actions first, and this component uses plain left-to-right order, which renders the same and keeps the source readable. Penpot's "Analysed2" appears to be a leftover duplicate and is not demoed; the second, unlabeled checkbox of "Check + Button" is reproduced as it is, with no invented purpose.

Layout (Figma flat table): the row is a flex container with align-items: stretch, so every cell is as tall as the tallest, like a real table row. Hover, focus-within and selected fills go on the cells, not the row, because hosts often lay rows out as display:contents inside a grid (so columns align across rows), and a display:contents element paints nothing. Selected is bg.surface-pressed; data-selected-fill="strong" on the table container uses the darker base/250 (Figma screen 25). Checkbox and save icons show only on hover, focus, selected or saved (the header row always shows them), and data-reveal-actions on the container dims row actions to 40% until hover or keyboard focus, so a long table reads as data first. A row's data-status colors its Status dropdown's value as a pill in the row-status tokens.

Selection: only a click on the row's own checkbox (a checkbox-cell containing [data-icon="checkbox"], so a drag handle in the same cell type is excluded) toggles data-selected; the checked icon swaps in by CSS. Shift+click selects the range from the last clicked row in the same table (visible rows in DOM order, so it follows sorting and skips rows hidden by a search), as one ds-table-row-select event with detail.range = true. A [data-checkbox-group] container may hold one select-all header cell (table-cell checkbox_role="select-all"), whose checked / semi / unchecked state follows how many rows are selected; clicking it selects all unless all are selected.

Reordering: a checkbox-cell holding Penpot's "Drag" glyph is a reorder handle. The row's own script uses native drag and drop, started only from the handle (draggable sits on the handle, which has a box even when the row is display:contents); dragover moves the row before or after the sibling under the pointer, measured on the sibling's first cell, and the dragged row's cells dim to 0.5 -- motion only as feedback. Hosts can drive their own drag and drop instead: data-dragging="true" dims a row, data-drop="before"/"after" draws an accent line on its top or bottom edge, and the whole handle cell shows the grab cursor. Not sourced from the design: selection, range selection, select-all and reordering. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. The `cells` list passes each cell's own props through to table-cell: type, content, icons, secondary_label, input_value, href, single_icon, single_icon_label, priority, checkbox_role, options, dropdown_label, view_label, tag_type, tag_subtype and article. Additions 2026-10-23: href makes the whole row a mouse target (pointer cursor on every cell), skipping clicks on controls, with modifier keys or while selecting text; the row-select checkbox cell is focusable (role=checkbox, aria-checked following data-selected) and toggles with Space / Enter through the same click path, with an accent focus outline. Cells now receive submit / extra_attrs and the other action props, so a host no longer builds action rows by hand. Action row (explicit request 2026-10-24): a table's one-action row (Add Project) answers hover like a row and shows the pointer, so the whole row is the target, not only its button. Visited (data-visited="true", explicit request 2026-10-24): a row the viewer has already acted on gets the faint bg-row-visited on its cells, lighter than hover, so touched and untouched rows tell apart; hover and selected still win. The host decides what marks a row and for how long; light only until a dark value exists. Current (data-current="true", explicit request 2026-10-25): the host marks the row of what it shows elsewhere right now (the project under the reader's eye in a preview beside the table); only its fill, one step lighter than hover (bg-row-current), tells it; icons and actions stay as on any row.
a11y_notes: Selection listens only on the row's checkbox cell, so clicks on other cells and their controls never collide with it. No row roles are added (role="row", aria-selected), since the system doesn't wrap rows in a role="table" structure; a host adds them at table level. Known gaps: the row checkbox and the select-all control are role="img" icons with aria-labels ("Select row", "Select all rows"), not real checkboxes, so their checked / mixed state isn't announced, and Shift+click range selection has no keyboard equivalent. The drag handle has aria-label="Reorder", but native drag and drop is pointer-only; an accessible reorder needs a keyboard path (e.g. arrow keys on the focused handle with a live announcement), not implemented. The second checkbox of "Check + Button" is labeled plainly "Checkbox". 2026-10-23: the checkbox cell is keyboard operable (Tab, Space, Enter) with aria-checked; a row href is only a larger mouse target, the link cell stays the keyboard path.

name: tag
description: A short label on a colored ground, for categories (accent-1/2/3), statuses (success, warning, danger) or a plain mark (neutral). Active is the solid, high-emphasis form; Passive the light tint for use in quantity, e.g. several tags in one row.

props.name: type
props.description: accent-1 | accent-2 | accent-3 | success | warning | danger | neutral. Sets data-type: which palette color the tag uses.

props.name: subtype
props.description: active (solid fill, white text) or passive (light tint fill, the type's strong color as text). Sets data-subtype. Figma calls these Acive / Passive.

props.name: label
props.description: The tag's text.

props.name: article
props.description: der | die | das: chooses the type by grammatical gender (der accent-1, die danger, das success) when `type` is not set. Other values fall back to accent-1.

rationale: Built from the Figma D_SYSTEM Tag set (node 103:4746): 4px padding (spacing-2), 1px radius (radius-md), body text. Color carries the meaning and nothing else does: each type maps to one palette family (accent primary/secondary/tertiary, signal success/warning/error, neutral). Active uses the strong color as fill; Passive uses the light tint with the strong color as text, so a passive tag keeps its hue at lower weight and several tags in a row stay readable without every one shouting. The colored types use the raw palette on purpose: a category or status color must mean the same in both themes. Neutral is the one theme-aware type (text.active / text.inverced / bg.surface-pressed / text.subactive), because black on the dark surface would disappear. Figma names the warning family 'caution'; this system calls it signal.warning. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Update 2026-10-23 (explicit request, "tags in dark are too strong"): passive colors moved to themed tokens (tag.<type>-bg / -text in Color-Base-Light / -Dark). Light is unchanged (the same palette tints and strong colors); dark uses each hue's darkest step as fill (blue.800, magenta.900, orange.900, green.900, yellow.900, red.800) and a light step as text, at least 6:1, replacing the light tints that glared on the black surface and accent-2's earlier dark exception. Active tags are unchanged. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Plain inline text in a span, no role: the label itself is the content and is read as text. Color is never the only carrier of meaning -- the label says what the tag is. Passive tags on the light tints keep the strong color as text; the lightest pairs (warning passive) are the lowest contrast in the set, so use warning passive for supplementary marks, not for the only statement of a warning.

name: text-button
description: An unfilled, text-only action control whose color shows the status of the operation behind it (active / loading / confirmed / disabled / error) rather than pointer emphasis -- used where a label must show an async action moving from in-progress to done (e.g. an inline row action). A permanent solid or dotted underline marks it as clickable and says whether the click leaves the page; hover and keyboard focus add '[ ]' brackets.

props.name: priority
props.description: primary (bold typography.buttonPrimary) or secondary (regular typography.buttonSecondary).

props.name: status
props.description: active, loading, disabled, confirmed, or error. status=active, error and disabled carry the permanent underline (see `underline` prop; disabled draws it in the disabled color, Figma D_SYSTEM node 132:4987) -- loading/confirmed are not pointer-interactive states and carry none. error is a destructive-action confirmation state, not a disabled one.

props.name: underline
props.description: solid or dotted -- the permanent underline drawn under the label for status=active, error and disabled: solid when the action navigates to a new page/URL, dotted when it stays within the current view (opens/closes a popup, loads more rows, expands a section). Chosen per instance by what the action does, not by eye (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions).

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon name (an icons/<name>.svg file), rendered in a `.ds-text-button__icon` span next to a `.ds-text-button__label` span, spacing-button-gap (5px) apart. The icon has no color of its own: it inherits the status color. Omit for a plain text button.

props.name: unread
props.description: data-unread="true": something new behind the button; secondary accent color.

props.name: icon_position
props.description: left or right: where `icon` sits relative to the label (Figma D_SYSTEM Button Type=Text+L-icon / Text+R-icon). right renders the label span first and sets data-icon-position="right". Ignored without `icon`.

props.name: icon_only
props.description: Render only `icon`, no visible label (Figma Type=Icon / icon-outlined). `label` becomes the button's aria-label and title and is required -- template.html fails the compose if it or `icon` is missing. data-icon-only="true"; 10px sides, 8px top/bottom (24px icon in Figma's 44x40 box).

props.name: outlined
props.description: 1px object-dark-passive border around the button (Figma Type=text-outlined / icon-outlined), taken out of the padding so an outlined button's outer box matches the plain one. data-outlined="true".

props.name: preview
props.description: hover: render the hover look (brackets, outlined accent border) without a pointer, via data-preview="hover". Documentation only -- for pages that lay every state side by side (Figma D_SYSTEM node 132:4987); never set it in product UI.

props.name: size
props.description: regular (unset) or small (data-size="small"): the box is as tall as one line of regular text, with no vertical padding, so a button can sit on a line of text without making its row taller. The 11px sides, brackets and underline are the regular button's. Text buttons only: icon_only and outlined keep their own boxes.

props.name: submit
props.description: Renders type="submit" so the button submits its enclosing form; otherwise type="button".

props.name: href
props.description: Renders an <a href> (through safe_url) instead of a <button>, for navigation. A disabled link has no href and carries aria-disabled.

props.name: article
props.description: der | die | das: tints an active label by grammatical gender (der keeps accent-1, die row-status-declined-text, das row-status-approved-text). Other values are ignored; only the active status is affected.

rationale:
Two independent axes, each carried by exactly one property so neither can be misread as the other. Priority changes only typography (typography.buttonPrimary bold vs buttonSecondary regular). Status changes only color, reusing the design's own status vocabulary: active = accent-1 (the one interactive color), loading = system.warning, confirmed = system.success, disabled = object-dark.active, error = system.error-strong where a theme defines it, falling back to system.error. error is a destructive-action confirmation step (e.g. gallery's 'Reset selection' arms a second click): the button is still clickable, the color says what the next click does. The Penpot source's tertiary priority was dropped: it was only partly defined.

Underline: permanent, not hover-only, because the design draws it at rest. It means 'clickable', so it is drawn for active and error; disabled keeps it in the disabled color so the control still says what it would do while the color says it can't; loading and confirmed are not clickable and carry none. solid vs dotted follows the system-wide convention (solid leaves the page, dotted stays in the view; see CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Solid is 1px (border-width-thin) so it doesn't turn into a bar under bold labels; dotted is 2px (border-width-default) because dot size follows thickness and 1px dots read as specks. The underline sits on an inner span (.ds-text-button__text, added by component.js for bare-text buttons, or .ds-text-button__label) because a browser paints an ancestor's text-decoration across its whole content box, which would include the bracket space.

Brackets: hover and keyboard focus reveal '[ ]' around the label -- the affordance the Penpot source drew on every instance, kept as an interaction cue only. They are always rendered but transparent at rest, so revealing them changes color only and the button never changes width. In tight contexts (header-block rows, sidebar set rows, action/link table cells, page-head, pane and popup-step heads, block-row actions, icon-only buttons) the brackets hang inside the horizontal padding instead of reserving space, so the button hugs its label and neighbours never shift. Outlined buttons show no brackets: their border turns accent-1 on hover and focus instead, the border already being the control's edge.

Box: no fill, no shadow, radius none -- the control is text and color already carries every state. Padding is spacing-cell (10px) vertical / spacing-button-x (11px) horizontal and the icon/bracket gap spacing-button-gap (5px), the figures Figma uses on every button, nav link and table action. Outlined adds the object-dark-passive hairline tables and cards already use, taken out of the padding so an outlined button's outer box matches a plain one. Icon-only buttons pad 8px top/bottom (spacing-3) and 10px sides (spacing-cell) around a 24px (spacing-7) glyph, the size used for standalone glyphs elsewhere.

Icons have no color of their own and inherit the status color, so they track every status without per-status rules; glyphs are inlined via fetch (see component.js) so currentColor applies. unread (accent-2, the nav dot's color) marks that something new is behind the button. preview='hover' draws the hover look statically, for documentation pages only. In dark, system.warning is yellow.600, so loading stays distinct from active. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Small (2026-10-19, explicit request, for the compact referent rows of CV): padding-block 0, so the height is the label line (1.2 x the button type size, the same 1.2 as body text) instead of 40px; nothing else about the button changes.
a11y_notes: Renders as a native <button>. status=disabled also sets the native disabled attribute, since the action is genuinely unavailable. status=loading stays focusable; a host that wants it inert while loading must also set disabled. The permanent underline is supplementary (color already distinguishes the statuses), so forced-colors modes that strip text-decoration remove no information. Icon variants keep .ds-text-button__icon aria-hidden="true": the label already supplies the full accessible name. The hover / focus brackets are CSS-generated ::before/::after content; browsers differ on whether generated content enters the accessible name, so the name never depends on it -- the button's own text is unchanged by hover or focus. Brackets also appear on :focus-visible, so keyboard users get the same affordance as a mouse hover.

name: toast
description: A short confirmation or error message, stacked top center (20px from the top edge), auto-dismissing. May carry one or two action buttons (e.g. links to something just generated). Created at runtime via window.dsToast.show(...), not pre-rendered markup -- see component.js.

props.name: message
props.description: The toast's text.

props.name: status
props.description: "default", "success", "warning" or "error". success, warning and error pick a color family (Figma D_SYSTEM Toster, node 103:4772): its medium color fills the toast, its strong color draws the border and the close square, text black. default is black with white text (2026-10-25).

props.name: actions
props.description: Optional array of {label, onClick} (onClick is only meaningful through the real window.dsToast.show() call, not this illustrative template -- see component.js). Up to two.

props.name: duration
props.description: Auto-dismiss delay in ms, only meaningful through window.dsToast.show(). The default (5000) is a judgment call, not a design-source value. 0 (explicit request 2026-10-01) never auto-dismisses: the toast stays until its close button is clicked.

props.name: progress
props.description: Only through window.dsToast.show(): a running task's progress line, 0-100, or null while it cannot be told (the line moves); omitted, no line. The returned update({message, progress}) changes it.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Only through window.dsToast.show(): called by the close button instead of dismissing, so the host can ask first and then call the returned dismiss().

rationale:
Styled to Figma D_SYSTEM's Toster (node 103:4772): a full status fill with a 1px border in the family's strong color, 20px system-message text, and a close button (a 24px square in the strong color with a white X). The fill carries the status at a glance; the X lets a reader drop a toast early instead of waiting out the timer. Figma draws success and warning; error follows the same pattern in the danger family. No shadow: the toast is edged by its border. Status colors are the fixed palette, as everywhere a color states a status, so the text is fixed black in both themes.

Behavior follows the product rule the component was built for: every action that changes stored data produces a short confirmation toast, every failed action an error toast naming the operation and the reason, toasts stack bottom right, 20px from both edges (explicit request 2026-10-25; top center before, after the Figma app artboard 345:10101), and auto-dismiss, and a toast may carry actions. Unlike every other component.js, which wires behavior onto markup a page already rendered, a toast only exists because an action just happened, so it exposes a runtime API (window.dsToast.show(...)). Hover and keyboard focus pause the dismiss timer and keep the time left, so a toast with actions doesn't vanish under a reaching cursor or a focused button. The 5000ms default duration is a judgment call; the rule states that toasts auto-dismiss, not how fast. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.

Actions (maintainer, 2026-10-13): a toast that carries actions has no close icon. The actions sit in the same row as the text, at the right, where the X would be; a toast without actions keeps the X. With actions the toast ends by an action or by its timer (duration 0 plus actions would never end, so a host does not combine them). Motion and the time line (explicit request 2026-10-25): a toast rises into place while fading in (240ms) and fades out sinking a little (180ms), so a new message is seen arriving and a leaving one does not just blink out; a spacing-1 line in the strong color along its bottom edge shrinks over the duration, showing how long the toast stays, and stops while the timer is paused. Both are functional (arrival, time left), and both are off under prefers-reduced-motion. Progress (explicit request 2026-10-25): a long task, such as an export, is followed in one toast with duration 0: show({ progress }) draws the same bottom line as a progress line (0-100, or moving while the share cannot be told), and the returned update({ message, progress }) changes its text and line until the host dismisses it; such a toast has no time line. Functional: the task's state stays visible while the reader works elsewhere. Default toast (explicit request 2026-10-25): black (base-1000) with white text, its edge and close square base-750 and its lines white, so it stands apart from the light greys of the page instead of sinking into them; its actions are white too. onClose (same date): the close button can ask the host first, which then dismisses or not. Update 2026-10-25 (explicit request): the default toast is white with black text on the dark page, the mirror of the black one on the light page, through the new tokens bg.toast and text.toast; its lines and actions follow text.toast, the edge and close square stay base-750.
a11y_notes: role="status" (not role="alert") on each toast: a polite announcement, because toasts report routine results rather than interrupting -- anything that must interrupt uses popup. Action buttons are real, focusable <button> elements from text-button's template. Auto-dismiss is mitigated for mouse (hover pause) and keyboard (focusin/focusout on the toast keeps it alive while an action inside it is focused). Remaining gap: a toast without actions offers nothing to focus, so a screen-reader user reading it gets no pause.
