The close button is a real <button> with aria-label="Dismiss" (the X is a CSS mask, no text).

name: tooltip
description: A hover/focus tooltip: add data-tooltip="..." directly onto any real element to give it one, no wrapper markup required. E.g. explaining why a disabled Undo button is disabled.

props.name: text
props.description: The tooltip's text. In real usage this is the data-tooltip attribute value on the actual trigger element (a button, an icon span, etc.) -- not a separate component instance. A line break in the text (a newline in the attribute value) starts a new line in the bubble, so one tooltip can carry a label, a text and a translation.

props.name: label
props.description: Only used by this component's own demo trigger (template.html): the visible content of the illustrative element data-tooltip is attached to. In real use, data-tooltip goes on an element the page already has; this prop has no meaning there.

props.name: preview
props.description: visible: data-preview="visible" on the [data-tooltip] element shows the tooltip without hover/focus. Documentation only (the site's Toasters and tooltips card); never in product UI.

props.name: data-tooltip-mode
props.description: On <html> or <body>, not on a trigger: 'layer' is accepted for pages written for the opt-in layer mode of 2026-10-23 and changes nothing, since every tooltip is the shared layer.

props.name: data-tooltip-delay
props.description: On <html> or <body>: milliseconds before a tooltip shows on that page. Unset: 1000. data-tooltip-instant on a trigger still skips it.

props.name: window.dsTooltip
props.description: show(box, text) shows host text at once at a box ({getBoundingClientRect}), e.g. a word inside a text; hide(); isTrigger(element); delay (ms, the page's show delay).

rationale: Styled to Figma D_SYSTEM's Tooltip (node 103:4777): a dark fill (tooltip-bg, Figma base/900), a 1px tooltip-border, white body text, 10px padding, no shadow -- dark so it reads as a layer above the page in either theme. Pure CSS, no JavaScript: content: attr(data-tooltip) reads the trigger's own attribute, and :hover / :focus-visible are the whole show condition, because a tooltip's dismissal is exactly 'stop hovering or focusing'. Adding JS (as popup and dropdown-menu need for their open state) would be complexity with no functional gain. Figma's text+icon variant is not implemented: the bubble is the host's ::after, and a host's ::before is already taken (text-button's hover brackets), so there is no free box for an icon. Known limitation: no viewport clamping, so a trigger near a container edge can render the bubble partly off-screen. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Update 2026-09-30 (explicit request): the bubble is at most a third of the viewport wide and wraps, and a small component.js keeps it on screen -- shifted inside the viewport edges, flipped below when it only fits there, and its text cut at the last word that fits, with an ellipsis, when it fits on neither side. Show/hide stays pure CSS; the script only measures and sets --_tooltip-shift, data-tooltip-placement and data-tooltip-clamped on the trigger. Update 2026-10-14 (explicit request, tooltips on every consumer button): a text button already draws its hover brackets on its own ::before and ::after, so the generic bubble turned the closing bracket into an empty dark box. On a .ds-text-button the bubble is the ::after of its label span (.ds-text-button__text / __label) instead, and component.js mirrors the text (and its cut) onto that span as data-tooltip-text / data-tooltip-text-clamped, because content: attr() on the span's pseudo-element reads the span's own attributes. The brackets are untouched. Update 2026-10-14 (explicit request): the bubble is shown one second after hover or focus (transition-delay: 1s on the shown state) and hides at once. data-tooltip-instant on the trigger skips that delay (the Summary cell's verdict). Update 2026-10-20 (explicit request, "tooltips always above any content"): the bubble is no longer the trigger's ::after. A single shared .ds-tooltip-layer, created and shown by component.js as a manual popover (top layer), is placed with position: fixed from the trigger's rect, so no overflow clip, sticky header or stacking context can cut it off. The 1 s show delay, data-tooltip-instant, the on-screen fit (shift, flip below, cut with an ellipsis) and the look are unchanged; they moved from CSS to the script, and the text-button label mirroring (data-tooltip-text) is gone. data-preview="visible" still draws an inline ::after for the documentation page. Merge with the opt-in layer mode of 2026-10-23 (another consumer's reading page): the shared top-layer bubble stays the one mechanism for every page, and that mode's additions are kept on it -- a text-button, header-tab or sort button whose label carries data-tooltip shows it for the whole button, data-tooltip-delay sets a page's delay, a line break in the text starts a new line (white-space: pre-line), and window.dsTooltip lets a host that explains words inside running text (no element per word) show its text on the same layer, so there is one tooltip mechanism and one look on the page. A host tooltip hides on scroll, resize, a click or a key, not when the pointer leaves. Left (explicit request 2026-10-24): data-tooltip-placement="left" on a trigger puts the bubble at its left, centred on its height, for a column of icon buttons at a page's right edge; with no room there it falls back to above / below.
a11y_notes: :focus-visible (not just :hover) shows the tooltip, so keyboard users reach it with Tab; so does keyboard focus on a control inside the trigger (:has(:focus-visible), 2026-10-03), for a tooltip set on a container such as a table cell around a button. The bubble has role="tooltip" but is not linked to its trigger; if the text must be announced, the host should add aria-describedby pointing at a real, visually hidden text node. A native <button disabled> can't receive focus, so a tooltip on a disabled button is mouse-only; to make it keyboard-reachable, the host would use aria-disabled on a still-focusable button instead of the disabled attribute.

name: word-token
description: A word inside a running text that the reader can look up: its state (in notes, already in the word list, open) shows as fill or underline, a hover or focus opens a card with lemma, translation and a grammar note, and a click is reported to the host. Also renders the legend of the states.

props.name: text
props.description: The word as it stands in the text. Plain text.

props.name: state
props.description: none | noted (bg-text-highlight fill) | known (dotted accent underline) | active (pressed fill and hairline outline: the word whose card is shown).

props.name: id
props.description: Unique per page; the card gets <id>-card and the word aria-describedby it.

props.name: card
props.description: {kicker, title, text, gloss, note, hint}, each optional plain text: kicker (lemma and part of speech, data role, uppercase), title (translation, heading-5), text (an explanation, body), gloss (second language, italic, subdued), note (grammar note for this occurrence, under a rule), hint (what a click does). No card: no popup.

props.name: interactive
props.description: true: a <button> that emits ds-word-token-click { text }. false: a focusable span whose card only explains (a marked run in a corrected sentence).

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Raw attributes on the word element (data-* ids the host reads back). Page-author markup only, never end-user data.

props.name: mode
props.description: 'legend' renders the legend instead of a word.

props.name: legend
props.description: With mode='legend': list of {state, sample, label}.

props.name: legend_hint
props.description: With mode='legend': a last item explaining hover and click.

rationale: From the application design canvas (2026-10-23), no Figma node. A word must stay part of its sentence, so it keeps the text's font, size and color; its relation to the reader's lists is shown by fill or line, never by color alone: noted is the bg-text-highlight fill (a marker pen over picked words), known is the dotted accent-1 underline (the system's 'clickable, stays on this view' line, CLAUDE.md Interaction conventions), active is bg-surface-pressed with a border-default hairline (the word the open card belongs to). Hover adds the pressed fill, the same hover the system's rows use, instead of brackets, which would push the sentence's words apart; that is the stated reason this control does not reuse text-button's bracket affordance. The card is tooltip's dark layer (tooltip-bg / -border / -text) so it reads as above the page in both themes, structured into the roles the content has (kicker in the data role at 60% opacity, translation in heading-5, gloss italic, note under a shadow-high rule, hint), because a plain tooltip's single text cannot carry them. Width 380px is the canvas's card width, clamped to the viewport. component.js places the card at fixed coordinates under the word (above when there is no room) so no scrolling container cuts it; without script it opens under the word by CSS. The 300 ms hover delay keeps cards from flashing while the pointer crosses a text; keyboard focus opens at once. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: An interactive word is a native <button> (Tab, Enter, Space); a non-interactive one is a focusable span. The card is role=tooltip and linked by aria-describedby, so a screen reader reads it after the word. Escape closes the card. The card never takes the pointer, so it cannot cover the next word's hover.
